91a458c2df591473:1947.summary: Fleet-level deployment of LLM agents creates un-undoable risks as agents autonomously move money, deploy code, and delete data while current security controls evaluate effects one at a time. To prevent agents from dangerously overdrawing risk under shared triggers, researchers propose the 'irreversibility budget'—a cumulative account of residual value-at-risk maintained by a trusted runtime across multiple principals, agents, and workflows. The runtime treats irreversibility as a primary resource, charging each action its residual loss and denying marginal effects once the aggregate budget would be overdrawn. Controlled studies demonstrate that per-effect gates can otherwise allow fleet-level overdraws of up to 48 times the tenant limit, whereas the budget successfully keeps correctly charged runs within bounds.
91a458c2df591473:1947.one_liner: The irreversibility budget runtime stops fleets of LLM agents from collectively overdrawing security limits when individual action gates pass.
91a458c2df591473:1947.bottom_line: Individual action controls allow LLM agent fleets to dangerously accumulate risk under shared triggers, making a cumulative runtime irreversibility budget necessary for safe deployment.

claims.text: We propose the irreversibility budget, a cumulative account of residual value-at-risk that a trusted runtime maintains for each principal across agents, workflows, and tenants.
claims.support_span: We propose the irreversibility budget, a cumulative account of residual value-at-risk that a trusted runtime maintains for each principal across agents, workflows, and tenants.

claims.text: We perform a controlled study in which per-effect gates admit fleet-level overdraws of up to 48 times the tenant's risk limit while the budget holds every correctly charged run within that limit.
claims.support_span: We perform a controlled study in which per-effect gates admit fleet-level overdraws of up to 48 times the tenant's risk limit while the budget holds every correctly charged run within that limit.

key_facts: Fleet-level overdraws prevented: up to 48 times the tenant's risk limit

0215029b1e45bbb5:2224.summary: Researchers evaluated the reliability of LLM agent self-reports and rationales by conducting an environment-grounded audit using an evolutionary Contexto search game where every guess receives an exact rank without human annotation. Across 200 runs generating 12,249 self-reports, the authors tested three common assumptions and found that all of them failed: stated confidence was uncalibrated, inherited rationales provided negligible benefit (roughly 250 ranks), and fitness-based selection produced no detectable transmission or selection differential in report accuracy. Specifically, operators overstated top-100 success rates by factors ranging from 4.8 to 9.3. The study concludes that LLM self-reports must be verified against their execution environment rather than trusted as evidence of agent reliability.
0215029b1e45bbb5:2224.one_liner: Auditing LLM agents via an environment-grounded search game shows their self-reports, confidence scores, and rationales are largely unreliable.
0215029b1e45bbb5:2224.bottom_line: LLM agent self-reports and confidence rationales drastically overstate success and cannot be trusted as metrics of internal reliability without direct environmental verification.

claims.text: We introduce an environment-grounded audit in which every intermediate proposal receives an exact outcome.
claims.support_span: We introduce an environment-grounded audit in which every intermediate proposal receives an exact outcome.

claims.text: Operators overstate top-100 success by factors of 4.8 to 9.3, while calibration and discrimination dissociate across model families.
claims.support_span: Operators overstate top-100 success by factors of 4.8 to 9.3, while calibration and discrimination dissociate across model families.

claims.text: Controlled interventions on 754 inherited rationales bound any measured benefit of the genuine rationale to roughly 250 ranks.
claims.support_span: Controlled interventions on 754 inherited rationales bound any measured benefit of the genuine rationale to roughly 250 ranks.

key_facts: Configurations tested: 5 configurations across 3 model families
Top-100 success overstatement factor: 4.8 to 9.3 times

3b369bcc6564570f:4122.summary: The cybercrime extortion group Clop has launched a mass-exploitation campaign using a critical zero-day vulnerability in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM software products, which are widely used in manufacturing, aerospace, and automotive supply chains. Tracked as CVE-2026-12569 with a capability for unauthenticated remote code execution, the flaw was disclosed by PTC on June 17, 2025, but was actively exploited by Clop as early as June to steal data from dozens of organizations including major publicly traded companies. ReliaQuest researchers discovered that Clop deployed a custom, purpose-built web shell and extortion framework designed specifically for Windchill that handles credential decryption, malware delivery, and lateral network traversal while mimicking standard application functions to evade detection. Toast and Zebra confirmed limited intrusions, while other alleged victims such as GE, Philips, and Shell did not respond.
3b369bcc6564570f:4122.one_liner: Ransomware group Clop is actively exploiting a critical RCE zero-day in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM software to steal data from global manufacturing and supply chain enterprises.
3b369bcc6564570f:4122.bottom_line: Organizations running PTC Windchill or FlexPLM must immediately hunt for custom web shells and signs of compromise as Clop leverages CVE-2026-12569 for widespread supply chain extortion.

claims.support_span: PTC disclosed the vulnerability — CVE-2026-12569 — on June 17 and issued a patch and initial indicators of compromise the following day.

27c4be7bea059c37:3552.summary: CISA has issued an urgent warning and ordered U.S. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to patch a critical remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions component, tracked as CVE-2026-33824, within three days under Binding Operational Directive 26-04. The flaw, caused by a double free in MS-IKEE, impacts all supported versions of Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server, allowing unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution over a network via UDP ports 500 or 4500. Microsoft addressed the vulnerability during the April 2026 Patch Tuesday release and recommended applying the security updates or blocking inbound traffic on unused ports as a workaround. CISA confirmed active exploitation in the wild, while recent weeks have also seen related ransomware exploitation of Windows Task Host and Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities.

27c4be7bea059c37:3552.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution on Windows systems via UDP ports 500 or 4500 through CVE-2026-33824, requiring immediate patching or firewall hardening.

claims.text: Tracked as CVE-2026-33824, this RCE vulnerability impacts all supported Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server releases, and it allows attackers without privileges to gain code execution by sending maliciously crafted packets to unpatched Windows systems through UDP ports 500 or 4500.

1df61faebdd15b1b:6299.summary: A developer discusses restructuring a collection of one-off Python security scripts into a unified, modular penetration testing toolkit to avoid code duplication and maintenance headaches. The toolkit splits architecture into a shared core handling HTTP requests, proxy support, and reporting, and individual modules containing specific vulnerability checks like path traversal, XSS, JWT analysis, IDOR, and endpoint discovery. A notable design choice built directly into the core HTTP client is automatic request pacing and rate-limit backoff (handling HTTP 429 status codes) to ensure politeness by default and compatibility with bug bounty requirements. adfad00b2087acdc:5745.summary: During a bug bounty engagement, a security researcher discovered a Host Header Injection vulnerability in a web application's password recovery workflow that led to Password Reset Poisoning and a 1-Click Account Takeover. By replacing the legitimate host header with an attacker-controlled Burp Collaborator ID during a password reset request, the application generated and emailed a valid password reset token embedded inside a URL pointing to the attacker's server. When the victim clicked the poisoned link, the complete reset token was transmitted to the attacker, who could then substitute it into the legitimate domain endpoint to set a new password and take over the account. Although the program marked the report as out of scope due to its exclusion policy for email hyperlink injection, the team acknowledged the risk and awarded a 100 CHF bonus.

42e867bb9487dafc:2589.summary: Researchers introduce FAIRY, a full-stack smart-agriculture agent system deployed on an operating soybean research farm at the Harbin Institute of Technology. 1b46e59ca26fa0d1:2131.summary: Researchers have uncovered context privilege escalation attacks against real-world AI agent harnesses, revealing security risks in vendor-proprietary context assembly designs. The study identifies two novel attack categories: MessageRole Context Privilege Escalation (M-CPE), where low-privileged content enters a higher-privileged message role, and Cross-Scope Context Privilege Escalation (X-CPE), where content persists beyond its intended scope. 8691ef02f4e8cc19:2532.summary: Researchers introduce DramaChain Bench, an end-to-end benchmark for short-drama generation that evaluates every stage of the production chain from script to finished video. 19514e9e8f81a627:2362.summary: Multi-model language services face significant challenges routing requests while respecting workload-level constraints due to high-dimensional prompt representations and nonstationary drift in request mixes and model performance. To address this, researchers propose Drift-Aware Sparse Routing (DRS), a routing policy that estimates rewards and resource usage from a rolling audit window using pessimistic reward and optimistic cost estimates. The approach applies a hard meter before commitment and provides formal theoretical guarantees on regret under sparse linear models and bounded drift. This framework optimizes multi-model language service delivery under strict computational and monetary budgets.

19514e9e8f81a627:2362.bottom_line: DRS provides a principled routing policy for multi-model LLM services that maintains strict resource budgets while adapting to request and model drift.

6f8bfb6d43d7b0af:2696.summary: An unauthenticated replication access vulnerability, CVE-2026-84700, affects PikiwiDB (Pika) v3.5.7. The database exposes an internal protobuf replication server on a port derived from the client port plus 2000 that fails to authenticate incoming requests. Although 'requirepass' is intended to protect replication, only the MetaSync handler validates it, while the frame dispatcher routes other requests without verification. This allows unauthenticated remote attackers to connect directly to the replication port, issue synchronization commands, obtain full snapshots and live write streams, and remove replica nodes.

6f8bfb6d43d7b0af:2696.bottom_line: PikiwiDB (Pika) v3.5.7 suffers from an unauthenticated replication access vulnerability that exposes full data sync streams and allows replica manipulation.

83711c63bda98155:2336.summary: Researchers introduce I-CARE, a methodology designed to formalize and evaluate interference-related phenomena in generative machine unlearning for text-to-image models. Machine unlearning aims to make AI models forget specific concepts, but often causes unintended degradation of related concepts that should be retained. Rather than introducing a new unlearning algorithm, I-CARE provides formal definitions for tasks, metrics, and reporting templates to enable reproducible study of interference across different unlearning settings. The framework is made available with an open-source implementation and a web-based graphical interface for exploring study outcomes.
83711c63bda98155:2336.one_liner: I-CARE provides a formal framework and open-source methodology for evaluating interference and concept degradation in text-to-image unlearning.
83711c63bda98155:2336.bottom_line: I-CARE standardizes the evaluation of concept interference in generative machine unlearning, separating long-term scientific analysis from transient empirical benchmarks.

claims.text: This paper introduces I-CARE, a methodology that formalizes interference as a first-class object of study in generative unlearning.
claims.support_span: This paper introduces I-CARE, a methodology that formalizes interference as a first-class object of study in generative unlearning.

claims.support_span: The software implementation of the methodology is provided in an open-source framework, together with a web-based graphical interface that enables exploration of the outcomes of this study without requiring direct interaction with the codebase or specialized data analysis tools.

8c2d2aa26b8bf1a9:2406.bottom_line: This protocol establishes a verifiable standard for agent memory integrity, which is critical for secure long-term agent operations.

99634fa2f7215b68:2526.summary: Researchers introduced mimeo, an open-source tool designed to compile public expert corpora into compact reference files and agent skills by extracting and verifying quotations against cached sources. Tested across eight logged builds, the tool averaged 38 model calls and successfully rejected 13.2% of extracted quotations via its verification checks. While mimeo answered 20 obscure, quotation-heavy questions better than closed-book models and avoided person-memory misstatements, testing on judgment transfer hit evaluation ceilings. The authors caution that mimeo serves as a reliable inspectable reference on a person rather than a proven transfer of their unique judgment.

04a197d7c2799f10:2604.summary: Researchers propose Defense-as-Skill, a runtime protection paradigm where an installable guard skill called SkillSonar runs alongside untrusted task skills to evaluate sensitive actions against user task boundaries. Using a newly constructed dataset called SCOPE-R covering 6 risk families and 206 malicious instances, the guard is evolved through a Monte-Carlo Tree Search procedure on rollout feedback. Across Claude Code and OpenClaw, SkillSonar significantly reduced attack success rates while maintaining utility, dropping in-distribution attack success from 0.482 to 0.104 and out-of-distribution success from 0.606 to 0.115 on GLM-5 runs. Ablations confirm that explicit safety responsibility assignment and skill-native representation are crucial for these security gains.
04a197d7c2799f10:2604.one_liner: SkillSonar implements a runtime guard as an installable agent skill, offering a trainable defense against malicious skill manipulation in LLM environments.
04a197d7c2799f10:2604.bottom_line: Evolving runtime guard skills via Monte-Carlo Tree Search provides robust protection against malicious tool actions without altering the base agent runtime.

claims.text: Our guard, SkillSonar, runs alongside untrusted task skills and checks sensitive actions against the user's task boundary, routing each action to an allow, replan, or confirmation decision without modifying the underlying agent runtime.
claims.support_span: Our guard, SkillSonar, runs alongside untrusted task skills and checks sensitive actions against the user's task boundary, routing each action to an allow, replan, or confirmation decision without modifying the underlying agent runtime.

bf437c8b0d8307c9:2506.summary: DeFi protocols expose depositors to substantial operational risk, totaling $9.45 billion across 1,075 events since 2020, yet lack mandatory capital requirements. Analyzing sector tail risks via a Basel loss-distribution approach reveals that bridge, derivatives, and residual sectors exhibit cyber-loss-level tails with point estimates past the infinite-mean boundary, while lending protocols require an estimated 18% TVL capital buffer for a 99.9% VaR. Although venues without buffers pay a higher median yield premium (125 bps), this market pricing falls drastically short of covering the actual operational tail risk. Because this unpriced risk disproportionately impacts retail depositors, the author recommends standardized loss disclosures and capital buffer transparency instead of regulatory capital mandates.
bf437c8b0d8307c9:2506.one_liner: DeFi operational risks remain severely underpriced by protocol yields, leaving retail depositors exposed to unhedged cyber and tail losses.
bf437c8b0d8307c9:2506.bottom_line: DeFi protocols fail to price operational risk adequately into deposit yields, shifting unhedged cyber-loss tails disproportionately onto retail users.

8afd4d0152d47f2f:2730.summary: Researchers introduce Revise, a validity-guided runtime engine designed to balance correctness and efficiency during concurrent online revisions in agent workflows. When a revision message is received, Revise intersects the delta with recorded data and control dependencies across the execution DAG to precisely target and invalidate affected tasks while preserving valid progress. Evaluated on coding-agent traces and applications built on LangGraph and LLMCompiler using Qwen3-14B, Revise reduces model calls by 40.6% to 56.0% compared to full restarts and by 31.3% to 43.6% compared to linear suffix recomputation. Under serving pressure, it also reduces tokens to correct completion by 13.26% and improves SLO goodput.
8afd4d0152d47f2f:2730.one_liner: Revise provides fine-grained workflow recovery for AI agents, cutting redundant model calls during concurrent task revisions.
8afd4d0152d47f2f:2730.bottom_line: Validity-guided runtime recovery allows agent workflows to process online revisions efficiently without discarding valid prior work or propagating stale states.

claims.text: We present \textsc{Revise}, a validity-guided runtime for fine-grained recovery in structured agent workflows.
claims.support_span: We present \textsc{Revise}, a validity-guided runtime for fine-grained recovery in structured agent workflows.

claims.text: On unmodified LangGraph and LLMCompiler applications using Qwen3-14B, it reduces model calls by 40.6--56.0\% relative to full restart and by 31.3--43.6\% relative to suffix recomputation.
claims.support_span: On unmodified LangGraph and LLMCompiler applications using Qwen3-14B, it reduces model calls by 40.6--56.0\% relative to full restart and by 31.3--43.6\% relative to suffix recomputation.

claims.text: Under serving pressure, it further reduces revision-to-correct-completion tokens by 13.26\% and improves SLO goodput by 3.07--5.43\%.

08ea06c8fadca153:2030.summary: Researchers introduce ISO-RAG, a geometry-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework designed to mitigate multi-hop question answering errors and latency issues caused by noisy global graph traversals. By projecting knowledge graphs into a hyperbolic Poincaré ball and precomputing node-wise isoperimetric profiles, ISO-RAG prunes spurious edges and restricts retrieval to a localized subgraph. This topological regulation of Personalized PageRank diffusion eliminates global traversal bottlenecks. Experiments on multi-hop QA benchmarks show that ISO-RAG achieves average absolute gains of 10.0% in retrieval recall and 4.3% in downstream exact match accuracy.
08ea06c8fadca153:2030.one_liner: ISO-RAG applies hyperbolic geometry to graph-based RAG, improving multi-hop retrieval precision and reducing latency.
08ea06c8fadca153:2030.bottom_line: Isoperimetric noise control in hyperbolic space prunes spurious knowledge graph edges, resolving the accuracy-latency trade-off in multi-hop RAG.

claims.text: Thus, we propose ISO-RAG (ISOperimetric Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a geometry-aware RAG framework.
claims.support_span: Thus, we propose ISO-RAG (ISOperimetric Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a geometry-aware RAG framework.

claims.text: Experiments on multi-hop QA benchmarks demonstrate that ISO-RAG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by average absolute gains of 10.0% in retrieval recall and 4.3% in downstream exact match, achieving a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off by fundamentally eliminating the latency bottleneck of global traversals.
claims.support_span: Experiments on multi-hop QA benchmarks demonstrate that ISO-RAG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by average absolute gains of 10.0% in retrieval recall and 4.3% in downstream exact match, achieving a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off by fundamentally eliminating the latency bottleneck of global traversals.

f1539e3b242f7b54:2415.summary: Researchers propose EvoFlint, an automated red-teaming framework that frames multi-turn LLM vulnerability discovery as an evolutionary search problem over conversation plans rather than raw prompt generation. Using LLM-driven mutation and crossover, a risk-indexed archive, and a generation-level memory, EvoFlint maps model failure modes across multiple conversational turns. When tested on the HarmBench split, EvoFlint achieved attack success rates of 35.8% on Claude Sonnet 4.6, 59.7% on GPT-5.4, 94.3% on Qwen3-32B, and 98.7% on GPT-4o. The resulting archives expose specific risk categories where model safety training remains deficient.
f1539e3b242f7b54:2415.one_liner: EvoFlint automates multi-turn LLM red-teaming via evolutionary search, exposing severe safety gaps across frontier models.
f1539e3b242f7b54:2415.bottom_line: Evolutionary quality-diversity search across multi-turn conversation plans uncovers systemic safety vulnerabilities in frontier language models.

8c4b47bf5feddd20:1822.summary: Researchers present AKRASIA, an inference-time backdoor attack targeting reasoning-based Code LLMs to achieve malicious code execution while evading human inspection and automated defenses. AKRASIA probes victim models to construct code-level backdoor triggers, employs in-context learning for backdoor embedding, and leverages model unfaithfulness to conceal triggers and generate plausible reasoning steps. Evaluations across 6 reasoning LLMs and 3 coding tasks demonstrated an average attack success rate of up to 99.34% while maintaining 97.23% task accuracy, successfully bypassing current defense methods and evading human inspection in up to 80% of settings.

8c4b47bf5feddd20:1822.bottom_line: Reasoning-based Code LLMs are vulnerable to stealthy inference-time backdoors that exploit model unfaithfulness to conceal malicious execution logic.

b31b96ee400813ef:2087.summary: Researchers introduce VoiceLongMemEval (VLME), a new benchmark evaluating AI assistants on long-horizon, multi-session dialogue histories where answers depend on paralinguistic metadata such as emotion labels, prosody descriptors, and voice events that cannot be recovered from text transcripts alone. Evaluating frontier and open-weight models revealed a pervasive affect gap; standard Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) pipelines systematically discard paralinguistic signals, while supplying text-track paralinguistic metadata yielded a 0.09 to 0.38 accuracy boost. Audio-native models successfully extracted these cues directly from speech, outperforming text-blind baselines.
b31b96ee400813ef:2087.one_liner: VoiceLongMemEval exposes the affect gap in conversational AI models, showing that standard ASR pipelines miss crucial paralinguistic metadata.
b31b96ee400813ef:2087.bottom_line: AI assistants evaluated on long-horizon audio dialogues fail unless audio-native models or paralinguistic metadata are used to bridge the affect gap.

8688f54cb8f6ce1d:2084.summary: The paper examines the evaluation of safeguards in deployed LLM services, arguing that traditional metrics like refusal rates, attack success rates, and policy violation rates only characterize local control performance rather than system safety. Because evidence requirements are asymmetric—a single successful bypass proves harmful help remains, while proving safety requires comprehensive system-wide evidence—local safeguard improvements do not automatically translate to a safer deployed system. The authors assert that safeguard research must account for how surrounding systems behave when attackers adapt or find alternative vectors.
8688f54cb8f6ce1d:2084.one_liner: Local LLM safeguard metrics do not guarantee overall deployment safety against adaptive attackers.
8688f54cb8f6ce1d:2084.bottom_line: Improving local LLM safeguard scores does not make a deployed system safer unless the surrounding system prevents bypasses under continuous adaptation.

claims.text: One attack that obtains harmful help from the deployed service suffices to establish that such help remains, and such attacks appear repeatedly in the coded record.

ed5e51101c875cd2:1228.summary: Readest, an open-source Tauri-based e-book reader, contains an 8.8 CVSS vulnerability in versions prior to 0.11.16 due to insufficient DOMPurify sanitization. Because DOMPurify treats iframe srcdoc contents as opaque strings, attackers can embed malicious HTML and scripts that run within the application's origin. This grants script execution access to Tauri IPC commands via parent.__TAURI_INTERNALS__, escalating to arbitrary code execution. Version 0.11.16 hardens sanitization by forbidding iframes, objects, embeddings, and the srcdoc attribute.
ed5e51101c875cd2:1228.one_liner: An iframe srcdoc sanitization flaw in Readest permits arbitrary code execution via malicious EPUB files.
ed5e51101c875cd2:1228.bottom_line: Updating Readest to version 0.11.16 is essential to block Tauri IPC command escalation via insecure EPUB HTML sanitization.

claims.support_span: Readest is an open-source e-book reader built on Tauri. In versions prior to 0.11.16, EPUB chapter HTML is sanitized with DOMPurify using a configuration that forbade only the <script> tag (FORBID_TAGS: ['script']) in apps/readest-app/src/services/transformers/sanitizer.ts.

claims.text: Script executing inside the iframe shares the parent origin and reaches Tauri IPC commands.
claims.support_span: The content iframe is configured with sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts", so script executing inside it shares the parent origin and can reach parent.parent.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke(...), giving access to every Tauri IPC command the application is permitted to use, which escalates to arbitrary code execution.

bef1acce9a8195ed:819.summary: WWBN AVideo contains a brute-force rate limiting bypass vulnerability in enforceRateLimit(), affecting login.json.php and 13 other endpoints. Because isBot() flags missing User-Agent headers or standard strings like 'curl' and 'bot' as bots, unauthenticated attackers can bypass rate limits entirely and execute unlimited password-guessing attacks.

claims.text: The isBot() function treats missing User-Agent headers as bots, causing cache layers to discard write attempts.
claims.support_span: The function stores its attempt counter via a cache layer (ObjectYPT::setCacheGlobal) that silently discards writes for any client identified as a bot by isBot(). Because isBot() treats a missing User-Agent header as a bot by default — and also matches common bot identifiers such as 'curl', 'bot', 'crawler', and 'spider' — the counter never increments for such clients, so the rate limit never fires.

key_facts: Affected software: WWBN AVideo (current e01e41ecc and earlier)

003de7da5fa7090e:31096.summary: OrcaReplay is an open-source tool and proxy system designed to record, replay, fork, and debug AI agent runs byte-for-byte with the network disabled. e40d26dc84add009:2074.summary: Skill-as-API is a protocol-layer coordination framework designed to protect the intellectual property of specialized skills in multi-agent software engineering systems. ccbaae25f31bc558:2550.summary: ToolGate is an executable acceptance pipeline designed to automate scientific benchmark construction requiring specialist software like FEniCSx. It uses a three-gate review process consisting of local script execution verification, randomized no-tool screening to filter out questions solvable without software, and a tool-using agent solver limit check. In a test instantiation with 500 generation attempts, the pipeline ultimately yielded 128 unique protocol survivors, successfully bridging repeatable answer checking with expert design.

a918b7d703aaf38a:2091.summary: APEx is a hierarchical experience utilization framework designed for deep research question answering that organizes interaction history into instance-level trajectory memories and category-level procedural skills. Optimized via a three-stage alternating GRPO training paradigm, the framework features a closed-loop architecture comprising an Executor, Distiller, and Planner. At test time, these distilled skills act as procedural priors for online reinforcement learning with skill-alignment regularization to prevent policy drift. Experiments demonstrate that APEx outperforms GPT-5.4 by 14.7 points across seven benchmarks.

276dbcb527e9837f:2142.summary: EvalDetectBench is an open pipeline and benchmark designed to measure evaluation awareness in frontier language models across Inspect-compatible evaluations. The benchmark uses a curated transcript suite to test whether models recognize when they are being evaluated and whether individual benchmarks leak evaluation markers. The authors reveal that systematic biases exist in the literature, where generator identity accounts for 11.25 percent of measurement variance and elicitation prompts vary widely across models. EvalDetectBench addresses these issues through per-model probe calibration and a stratified generator-harmonisation procedure.

276dbcb527e9837f:2142.bottom_line: EvalDetectBench uncovers and corrects systematic measurement biases caused by model evaluation awareness in AI safety frameworks.

1a15740211f46341:2268.summary: AGENTSCOPE is a neuro-symbolic approach designed to diagnose failures in LLM agents by converting complex interaction trajectories into structured behavioral abstractions. The method specifies agent property behaviors using neural invariants and leverages LLM-guided reasoning against these abstractions to pinpoint the exact failure step and category. Tested on the Who&When dataset and a custom dataset named AgentErrata, AGENTSCOPE outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in fault localization and attribution accuracy. This framework demonstrates that structured abstractions can enable reliable, interpretable agent debugging.

3733ca5e7ba69bd4:2439.summary: Loom is a generative consensus framework for real-world Root Cause Analysis that aggregates open-form hypotheses emitted by modular diagnostic heuristics. By projecting textual hypotheses into a continuous embedding space and resolving conflicts via an iterative centroid-based reweighting algorithm, Loom feeds a single lightweight LLM synthesis step. Evaluations on the OpenRCA benchmark show that Loom matches state-of-the-art autonomous agents on multiple datasets while operating roughly 26 times faster with a single LLM call per incident. This deterministic consensus approach reduces inference latency and fosters trust among subject matter experts.

f56ff34eda81c59a:2593.summary: ACLE-MCP is an invocation-scoped architecture for remote Model Context Protocol services that addresses the post-authorization execution trust gap by combining delegated authorization, workload appraisal, and resource-side execution admission. ebbf32604ed1e910:2715.summary: Persistent memory in LLM agents introduces a 'Memory Trust Gap' where stale stored facts can override current authoritative tool evidence, leading to capability-dependent over-trust. 4082ab78f2b07f4c:2703.summary: Multi-agent AI systems often spawn multiple agents to improve inference, but duplicated reports derived from the same underlying evidence create an epistemic Sybil problem. Controlled tests with over 20,000 LLM-agent extraction calls show that increasing report multiplicity while holding evidence roots fixed collapses naive posterior coverage from 0.940 down to 0.263. Conversely, increasing evidence-root multiplicity while holding report counts steady properly closes the gap, proving that collective inference must track evidential ancestry rather than agent or report similarity.

4082ab78f2b07f4c:2703.bottom_line: Spawning multiple AI agents does not improve accuracy if reports share the same evidence root, necessitating evidential ancestry tracking.

c344f2b6cc3a74c2:2550.summary: PROSE (Provenance through Relational Organization of Semantic Expression) is a black-box model fingerprinting method that verifies LLM ownership through semantic structures rather than brittle query-key associations. Instead of relying on specific tokens or memorized responses, PROSE encodes ownership within how a model semantically organizes its in-domain conclusions using a private bank of semantic templates internalized via mixed fine-tuning. Experiments across multiple architectures show that PROSE achieves a 100 percent fingerprint detection rate without false positives while preserving model utility under downstream modifications and quantization.

f4a30a30a2bb572b:2081.summary: Potential-Guided Policy Optimization (PGPO) is a group-based reinforcement learning method designed for multi-turn agentic tasks with sparse terminal rewards. To overcome the limitation where trajectory-level outcomes leave intermediate actions in failed trials poorly differentiated, PGPO estimates empirical state potentials from anchor-state-group return statistics. It derives action advantages from potential differences between adjacent states, enabling cross-trajectory credit propagation and finer-grained step-level credit assignment. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop demonstrate strong performance improvements and informative failure-side credit signals with negligible overhead.

b50a999693a8d100:2198.summary: Long-running LLM agents rely on persistent memory to carry state, but errors or misrepresentations in memory can lead to 'endogenous authorization laundering' where spurious permissions are generated without external attacks. Requiring source event backing and event sourcing mitigates laundering but introduces safety-utility trade-offs.

b50a999693a8d100:2198.bottom_line: Persistent memory acts as an implicit authorization policy in LLM agents, where memory errors lead to autonomous authorization laundering and unauthorized actions.

claims.support_span: When memory misrepresents this evolving authorization state, the agent's own records can grant authority that the underlying history never permitted, resulting in misaligned behavior without any external attacks.

959b31dbbded7b8e:2366.summary: Researchers have introduced UTP-Bench, a large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate uncertainty-aware travel planning in LLMs using real-world travel data from 504 Indian cities. Traditional benchmarks assume deterministic conditions, whereas UTP-Bench incorporates empirical delay distributions and crowd-density patterns to model realistic disruptions. It evaluates itineraries using three novel metrics: Buffer Adequacy Score (BAS), Crowd-Aware Timing Score (CATS), and Transport Delay Absorption Score (TDAS). Experiments using models such as GPT-5, Qwen3, Mistral, and Phi-4 demonstrate significant gaps in temporal buffering and delay-aware transportation scheduling. This benchmark helps developers assess and improve the robustness of travel-planning agents under stochastic real-world conditions.
959b31dbbded7b8e:2366.one_liner: This new benchmark for Indian travel data helps developers evaluate whether LLM-generated itineraries survive real-world transit delays and crowd variability.
959b31dbbded7b8e:2366.bottom_line: Current state-of-the-art LLMs struggle with stochastic real-world travel disruptions, which can be measured systematically using UTP-Bench.

claims.support_span: The dataset integrates real-world travel data spanning 504 cities of India, including attractions, restau- rants, accommodations, and multi-modal trans- portation networks.

d0acfb1a93a00dd5:2698.summary: Researchers have introduced the Reliable Enterprise Agent Deployment (READY) framework to qualify AI agents for enterprise workflows based on reliability, human oversight burden, and cost. Rather than relying solely on autonomous benchmark accuracy, READY measures how a human-AI system performs under specific oversight policies and statistically qualifies it on held-out cases. A clinical-audit case study involving 16 agent systems and 750 cases revealed that models with similar autonomous accuracy can require vastly different amounts of human review to meet identical reliability targets. The open testbed allows developers to establish explicit, testable operating points for enterprise deployment decisions.
d0acfb1a93a00dd5:2698.one_liner: The READY framework gives developers a systematic way to measure the human oversight cost and reliability required to deploy AI agents in enterprise workflows.
d0acfb1a93a00dd5:2698.bottom_line: Autonomous benchmark accuracy hides the true human review burden required to safely deploy AI agents in production enterprise environments.

claims.text: In an end-to-end clinical-audit case study spanning 16 agent systems and 750 cases, READY reveals differences hidden by autonomous performance: two systems separated by only 0.3 points in autonomous accuracy (72.8% vs. 72.5%) require 39.2% versus 29.6% human review, respectively, to qualify at the same 76% reliability target under the evaluated oversight policy.
claims.support_span: In an end-to-end clinical-audit case study spanning 16 agent systems and 750 cases, READY reveals differences hidden by autonomous performance: two systems separated by only 0.3 points in autonomous accuracy (72.8% vs. 72.5%) require 39.2% versus 29.6% human review, respectively, to qualify at the same 76% reliability target under the evaluated oversight policy.

da3f4917b4286a42:2184.summary: Researchers have introduced predicted-state matching, a training objective designed to align web agent world models with downstream rankers by ensuring predicted states can distinguish true outcomes from alternative actions. Traditional world models are trained via supervised next-state prediction, producing representations that often fail to help rankers accurately score candidates. Using a branching web-agent dataset derived from WebArena Go-Browse trajectories, the authors trained models that outperform standard supervised next-state prediction baselines. This approach improves Process Reward Model action ranking on WebPRMBench and increases end-to-end task success on WebArena-Lite.
da3f4917b4286a42:2184.one_liner: Predicted-state matching improves web agent action selection by training world models to discriminate between alternative candidate states rather than just predicting the next state.
da3f4917b4286a42:2184.bottom_line: Training web agent world models to distinguish alternative outcomes directly improves test-time action ranking and end-to-end task success.

claims.text: Experiments on our held-out predicted-state matching benchmark show that our approach outperforms world models trained with supervised next-state prediction.
claims.support_span: Experiments on our held-out predicted-state matching benchmark show that our approach outperforms world models trained with supervised next-state prediction.

6e0dd4fe2caa5073:3062.summary: A vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-81928, has been discovered in Net::DNS versions before 1.57 for Perl, allowing memory exhaustion via unbounded recursion in sig_data. The issue occurs when re-encoding a message containing a misplaced TSIG record in the answer or authority section, which bypasses removal checks and triggers infinite signing recursion. Because each cycle re-encodes the whole message, fewer than 100 bytes on the wire can exhaust available memory and crash forwarding or proxy processes. Administrators should upgrade to Net::DNS 1.57 or apply a workaround to reject messages where TSIG records appear outside the final position of the additional section.
6e0dd4fe2caa5073:3062.one_liner: Update Perl's Net::DNS to version 1.57 to patch a memory exhaustion vulnerability caused by unbounded recursion when handling misplaced TSIG records in proxies or forwarders.
6e0dd4fe2caa5073:3062.bottom_line: Unpatched Net::DNS versions below 1.57 allow remote processes to crash via memory exhaustion using malformed packets under 100 bytes.

claims.text: Net::DNS versions before 1.57 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded recursion in sig_data when re-encoding a message with a misplaced TSIG record.
claims.support_span: Net::DNS versions before 1.57 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded recursion in sig_data when re-encoding a message with a misplaced TSIG record.

key_facts: Vulnerable versions: Net::DNS before 1.57 for Perl

ad54e2d6867ca789:1521.summary: As enterprise platforms transition to conversational reasoning interfaces, the stateless nature of LLM APIs creates an architectural gap. While statelessness enables horizontal scalability for AI providers, it forces client applications to manage the entire burden of conversational state and semantic memory. The work identifies the Hydration Proxy Pattern, an architecture that decouples session persistence from the reasoning engine. The framework ensures platform sovereignty over conversational data while enabling secure, multi-stage semantic grounding.
ad54e2d6867ca789:1521.one_liner: A new architectural pattern helps decouple session persistence from stateless LLM APIs to maintain sovereign control over conversational state.
ad54e2d6867ca789:1521.bottom_line: The Hydration Proxy Pattern resolves the architectural tension between stateless LLM APIs and enterprise conversational session persistence.

403a19d9ee1ed052:2702.summary: Autonomous agents can already pay per request through protocols like x402, but atomic and final transactions fail in agent commerce where delayed fulfillment requires escrow. The Agentic Settlement Protocol (ASP) introduces an application profile over on-chain authorize-and-capture escrow for businesses whose fulfillment is confirmed off-chain. ASP provides a three-deadline hold model, a fulfillment-verification ladder, engine-authoritative partial refunds, and exposure controls to bound credit risk on stablecoin rails. The design is intended to let independent implementations interoperate and is instantiated on the XDC Network.
403a19d9ee1ed052:2702.one_liner: The Agentic Settlement Protocol brings escrow-based authorize-and-capture commerce to autonomous agents on stablecoin rails.
403a19d9ee1ed052:2702.bottom_line: Autonomous agent commerce requires delayed-fulfillment escrow models rather than atomic per-request payments to safely handle real-world transactions.

claims.support_span: Autonomous agents can already pay per request: HTTP-native protocols such as x402 let an agent sign a stablecoin authorization and receive a resource in the same round trip.

claims.text: We present the Agentic Settlement Protocol (ASP), an application profile over on-chain authorize-and-capture escrow for businesses whose fulfilment is confirmed off-chain.
claims.support_span: We present the Agentic Settlement Protocol (ASP), an application profile over on-chain authorize-and-capture escrow for businesses whose fulfilment is confirmed off-chain by their own order, scheduling, invoicing or booking system, abstracted as a fulfilment engine.

ed86fd6148398014:2624.summary: Linux kernel vulnerabilities pose critical risks, but a fundamental challenge in automated exploitation is the conceptual gap between abstract strategies and concrete operations. To bridge this, researchers introduce PrimSynth, a multi-agent framework that formalizes six classes of exploit primitives and utilizes an iterative closed loop to synthesize exploitation chains. Operating through vulnerability-directed execution in a rebootable validation environment, PrimSynth was evaluated on 16 real-world Linux kernel CVEs spanning five vulnerability types. Experimental results demonstrate a 100 percent primitive match rate and an 82.4 percent strategy synthesis rate when public PoCs are available.
ed86fd6148398014:2624.one_liner: PrimSynth automates the discovery, validation, and synthesis of exploit primitives for Linux kernel memory corruption vulnerabilities.
ed86fd6148398014:2624.bottom_line: Multi-agent frameworks can systematically automate Linux kernel exploit primitive synthesis with high reliability when validation environments are present.

7975825d3c277925:1889.summary: Human interventions at critical fault points during AI agent conversations can significantly alter diagnostic accuracy in multi-agent medical systems. Using the MedQA dataset to analyze simulated doctor-patient conversations, correct interventions improved baseline diagnostic accuracy by up to 40 percent. Conversely, incorrect or bias-related interventions degraded performance by up to 6 percent while increasing diagnostic drift and uncertainty. The findings show that identifying and guiding fault points with human interventions can improve diagnostic robustness.

7975825d3c277925:1889.bottom_line: Human-in-the-loop interventions at precise reasoning fault points are crucial for correcting and stabilizing multi-agent medical diagnoses.

cc520597c7111d25:1999.summary: Automated video interview assessment faces challenges due to high applicant volumes and the opacity of existing AI scoring methods. To address this, researchers introduced PhoenixNest-Video, an evidence-grounded multimodal agent framework that builds a semantic video graph as structured working memory. The framework performs rubric-conditioned retrieval with cross-modal verification across visual, audio, and textual streams to generate traceable per-criterion scores. Evaluated on VInterview-2025, PhoenixNest-Video achieves 91.50 percent grade-level accuracy while remaining compact and exposing underlying evidence for human review.

cc520597c7111d25:1999.bottom_line: Evidence-grounded multimodal agent frameworks can match expert panel evaluations in video interviews while providing transparent rationales.

12c0e4182d63fef3:2133.summary: Generative engine optimization (GEO) can be weaponized by adversaries to inject targeted misinformation into LLM-synthesized search answers. To evaluate defenses against this threat, researchers created Counter-GEO-Bench, a benchmark containing 247 human-verified queries paired with information-distorting GEO rewrites. Off-the-shelf safety-taxonomy guardrails like Granite Guardian, Llama Guard 3, and NeMo Self-Check Fact-Checking reduce attack success rates by at most 5.7 percent because misinformation passes through them as fluent text. However, a lightweight benchmark baseline called C-GEO Guard reduces attack success rates by 47.6 percent relative with near-zero utility loss.
12c0e4182d63fef3:2133.one_liner: Counter-GEO-Bench evaluates defenses against information-distorting generative engine optimization attacks in LLMs.
12c0e4182d63fef3:2133.bottom_line: Standard LLM safety guardrails fail to catch generative engine optimization misinformation, requiring specialized factual verification layers.

2ccf01f9cb19b9fa:2326.summary: Safety alignment in large language models largely focuses on surface forms, leaving models vulnerable to recontextualization attacks that bypass refusals. The ASCII Attack embeds fully legible harmful requests within ASCII-art characters and frames them as artistic critique to request feedback. Tested across eleven models and eight harm topics, a harm-aware classifier judged 62 percent of framed prompts as harmful compared to 42 percent of direct controls, with the most susceptible model succeeding 93 percent of the time. The effect demonstrates that formatting content as creative critique easily subverts safety guardrails.

2ccf01f9cb19b9fa:2326.bottom_line: Surface-level safety alignment fails against semantic recontextualization attacks that frame harmful prompts as artistic feedback.

b88095b3f44a2fd9:2538.summary: Persistent AI agents construct autobiographical state through reflection and retrieval, but stored material does not inherently carry valid epistemic standing. Untrusted inputs and prompt injections can infiltrate persistent state and be treated as legitimate agent history or user commitments. To solve this, researchers introduce typed provenance and assertion guardrails enforcing autobiographical assertion boundedness. An evaluated conformance suite showed that typed mediation successfully blocked unsafe opportunities while maintaining valid controls, outperforming flat and source-tag comparison rules.

36cfcc22ca58f549:2000.summary: Visual modalities enhance multimodal large language models (MLLMs) but introduce cross-modal safety drift, where a benign textual query conveys harmful intent when paired with a specific image. Pilot studies show that safety response rates for such requests are substantially lower than for explicit text because visual cues receive limited model attention and weakly trigger refusals. To mitigate this, researchers propose safety-awareness representation transfer (SRT), a lightweight direction-refinement method using a frozen MLLM backbone. Experiments show SRT effectively improves safety across diverse cross-modal settings while preserving model utility.
36cfcc22ca58f549:2000.one_liner: Safety-awareness representation transfer (SRT) mitigates cross-modal safety drift in multimodal large language models.
36cfcc22ca58f549:2000.bottom_line: Multimodal LLMs suffer from cross-modal safety drift that can be corrected via lightweight representation transfer without unfreezing the backbone.
