9e93fdefd59e2bf0:2315.summary: Researchers have revealed a new attack method called the Neutral Prompting Attack (NPA), which exploits LLM-powered coding agents by covertly increasing package hallucination rates. By providing semantically benign instructions that encourage imagination or exhaustiveness, NPA shifts models toward generating speculative, non-existent package names without explicit malicious phrasing. Threat actors can register these hallucinated package names to execute supply chain attacks against downstream users. Evaluations showed that NPA consistently increases package installation attack success rates while successfully bypassing static, LLM-based, and agent-based skill defenses.
9e93fdefd59e2bf0:2315.one_liner: Neutral Prompting Attacks covertly steer LLM coding agents into hallucinating fake packages to enable software supply chain exploits.
9e93fdefd59e2bf0:2315.bottom_line: Harmless-looking prompts can systematically drive coding agents to hallucinate non-existent packages, enabling typosquatting supply chain attacks.

claims.text: Neutral Prompting Attacks use semantically benign prompts to increase package hallucination propensity in coding agents.
claims.support_span: In this paper, we introduce \emph{Neutral Prompting Attack} (NPA), a highly stealthy attack paradigm in which semantically benign instructions, such as encouraging imagination and exhaustiveness, increase package hallucination propensity without containing explicit malicious intent.

claims.text: NPA bypasses existing static, LLM-based, and agent-based security defenses.
claims.support_span: Our results show that NPA increases both \emph{Hallucination ASR} and \emph{Pip Install ASR}, changes the distribution of hallucinated package names, and evades existing static-analysis, LLM-based, and agent-based Skill defenses.

key_facts: Impact: Software supply chain package hallucination
Defenses bypassed: Static analysis, LLM-based, and agent-based Skill defenses

0f3d055b03df47be:2914.summary: A denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2026-16028) has been disclosed in the Protocol::HTTP2 Perl distribution in versions prior to 1.14. When an HTTP/2 stream reaches the closed state, residual entries are retained indefinitely in the connection stream table, bypassing SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS boundaries. A malicious peer can open and close streams sequentially, consuming roughly 920 bytes per stream and exhausting server memory (approx. 88 MiB per 100,000 requests). Administrators must upgrade to version 1.14 or mitigate by closing connections after a fixed number of requests.
0f3d055b03df47be:2914.one_liner: Protocol::HTTP2 for Perl before 1.14 suffers from a memory exhaustion flaw (CVE-2026-16028) via unbounded closed stream tables.
0f3d055b03df47be:2914.bottom_line: Upgrade Protocol-HTTP2 to 1.14 to prevent unauthenticated remote peers from causing memory exhaustion via sequential stream creation.

claims.text: Protocol::HTTP2 before 1.14 retains closed stream entries indefinitely in the connection stream table.
claims.support_span: Protocol::HTTP2 versions before 1.14 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via closed streams that stream_state never removes from the connection stream table.

claims.text: Sequential streams cause memory leaks of roughly 920 bytes per stream, accumulating ~88 MiB over 100,000 streams.
claims.support_span: Measured against a server built on this module, roughly 920 bytes are retained per closed stream for about 19 bytes on the wire, so 100,000 sequential streams on one connection grow server resident memory by about 88 MiB.

key_facts: Impact: ~88 MiB memory leak per 100,000 streams (920 bytes/stream)

claims.support_span: Experiments on the Who&When benchmark across six LLMs show that DCFA improves step-level accuracy by up to 8.27% over state-of-the-art baselines.

9d25417a3d92c202:2028.summary: A study investigating LLM agents in simulated financial markets finds that increasing model capability can increase systemic market risk due to correlated decision-making. While correlated reasoning reduces market volatility under accurate conditions, it drastically amplifies collective risk when models are exposed to shared misinformation.

04fce0395d5d8b0c:2433.summary: Researchers proposed a hybrid framework that integrates bounded behavioural rubrics and structured scenario specifications into a calibrated agent-based model of solar photovoltaic adoption by Irish dairy farms. The approach preserves original techno-economic adoption mechanisms while adding bounded behavioural modulation and scenario-driven uncertainty analysis. Tested across multiple policy settings, Monte Carlo worlds, and random seeds, the model demonstrated stable, economically plausible behaviour with adoption outcomes remaining bounded and monotonic. The framework achieved up to roughly 13% behavioural adoption increase relative to the corresponding logistic case without producing unstable or unrealistic saturation dynamics. This demonstrates that LLM-assisted specifications can be integrated into calibrated energy agent-based models in a controlled and reproducible manner.

6746df268b68cea3:2362.summary: Researchers formalized execution-state unlearning for stateful long-running LLM agents, proving that exact unlearning requires recomputing transitions from the target injection step. Because standard deletion leaves cached artifacts and derived summaries tainted, memory deletion fails to prevent leakage and instruction-based forgetting collapses under elicitation. The authors introduce Provenance-Guided Selective Replay, a cross-layer contract spanning prompts, compressed memory, and the KV cache that uses provenance graphs to pinpoint injection points and crops the cache for sanitized replay. Audited across various models and benchmarks, selective replay achieves performance indistinguishable from a full reset while requiring up to nine times fewer recomputed tokens.

6746df268b68cea3:2362.bottom_line: Standard memory deletion leaves stateful LLM agent histories tainted, but provenance-guided selective replay achieves exact unlearning efficiently.

0fb30158214d8a71:2757.summary: Researchers investigated post-violation recovery admission for LLM tool agents and identified the scalar projection trap, where aggregate-score gates commit trajectories to suboptimal plateaus. The authors introduced SiLR, a framework that shadow-executes proposals and admits them under a product order over branch-level violation states. Proving that no scalar surrogate is sound for this order, the authors demonstrated that SiLR successfully recovered 21 out of 21 multi-action episodes on mined Gym-ANM scenarios, outperforming scalar and support-only baselines. Furthermore, when used as a GRPO process reward, SiLR outperformed count projection and was the only tested reward whose ungated policy exceeded the untrained base.

0fb30158214d8a71:2757.bottom_line: Scalar projection gates fail to handle complex multi-constraint LLM tool agent violations, making structure-preserving product-order admission necessary.

8d2976e97142af04:2445.summary: Security-critical context in LLM agent systems can often be dropped, widened, or reinterpreted across component boundaries, creating a failure mode known as security-context discontinuity. To address this, researchers introduced CONTINUITY, a framework that models system components using assume-guarantee contracts and carries authenticated security contexts via signed root grants and execution permits. In evaluations covering 2,560 parameterized attack instances across 32 fault classes, the full CONTINUITY configuration prevented harmful external effects while completing all benign tasks.
8d2976e97142af04:2445.one_liner: CONTINUITY offers an architectural pattern for preserving security context across agentic tool calls and multi-component LLM workflows.
8d2976e97142af04:2445.bottom_line: Composable LLM agent controls require explicit assume-guarantee contracts to prevent authorization bypasses across component boundaries.

claims.text: We identify this failure mode as security-context discontinuity and introduce CONTINUITY, a framework for verifiable composition of agent security controls.

677ae0a272ee71fd:1683.summary: Current LLM safety evaluations often rely on binary metrics that fail to capture nuances across varying threat implicitness levels. Researchers have introduced TIER, a Threat Implicitness Benchmark designed to assess open-weight LLMs across four risk domains and four threat levels ranging from explicit prompts to sophisticated jailbreaks. 33365a5b4da124e9:2259.summary: Researchers have proposed CoSkill, a unified multi-agent reinforcement learning framework designed to resolve structural shortcomings in skill-based LLM agent learning. Instead of treating skill libraries as passive objects or static workflows, CoSkill introduces a learnable Meta-Skill Agent jointly trained with a Reasoning Agent over a hierarchical skill library using a shared backbone. This architecture enables end-to-end co-adaptation, where task performance guides the Meta-Skill Agent in refining step skills utilized by the Reasoning Agent. 17ca31ccb3d23aca:2367.summary: Researchers formulated solar photovoltaic (PV) policy design as a sequential decision problem by integrating reinforcement learning (RL) with a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) that simulates yearly adoption under uncertainty. 54217c49ff17cf31:5492.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered PEEP, a complex Chromium-based post-exploitation framework that disguises itself as a legitimate bookmarks extension named "Smart Bookmarks" in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge. PEEP requires prior administrative privileges or code execution to install, after which it bypasses Web Store security checks and user prompts by manipulating Chromium's Secure Preferences integrity values. It communicates with its command-and-control server over plaintext HTTP every 30 seconds to exfiltrate browsing telemetry and session cookies, while utilizing an auxiliary native-messaging executable ("nm_host.exe") to execute host-level shell commands and manage files. Built upon foundations derived from the open-source RedExt framework, the malware relies on sideloading, enterprise force-install policies, and a ScriptCache fallback to maintain persistence. Although unassigned to a specific nation-state actor, Chinese-language artifacts found within its source code point toward a Chinese-speaking threat group.

54217c49ff17cf31:5492.bottom_line: Compromised Chromium browsers can be turned into persistent host backdoors via the PEEP toolkit, which leverages native messaging bridges to execute arbitrary OS commands.

aefc80c094c3990d:2451.summary: Researchers proposed FedIoC, a federated learning framework that enables cross-organizational attack campaign detection without sharing sensitive telemetry or raw threat indicators. Local clients train on IoC-matched network flows using a supervised contrastive loss, which aligns threat patterns directly within gradient directions. The central server clusters incoming gradient updates by cosine similarity to group correlated campaign activity across distributed institutions holding disjoint indicator sets. Tested on two public threat detection benchmarks, FedIoC demonstrated that non-IID gradient structures allow servers to identify coordinated multi-organization campaigns without direct indicator transmission.
aefc80c094c3990d:2451.one_liner: FedIoC leverages contrastive federated learning gradients to detect multi-organizational cyber campaigns without sharing private threat intelligence.
aefc80c094c3990d:2451.bottom_line: FedIoC allows distributed security teams to correlate multi-enterprise cyberattack campaigns via gradient cosine similarity while keeping threat indicators confidential.

claims.text: FedIoC uses a supervised contrastive loss on local IoC-matched flows to encode attack campaign patterns into gradient updates.
claims.support_span: We propose FedIoC, a modular framework in which clients fold locally available structured threat indicators into their gradient updates; we instantiate the client-side encoder with a supervised contrastive loss over IoC-matched flows.

claims.text: The central server clusters client updates by cosine similarity to identify cross-organization campaigns without receiving indicators.
claims.support_span: Clients sharing indicators for the same attack campaign then produce aligned gradient components, which the server clusters by the cosine similarity of their updates to recover global campaign patterns without any direct IoC transmission.

key_facts: Clustering metric: Cosine similarity of gradient updates
Evaluation benchmarks: Two public threat-detection benchmarks

d0f7619855def175:2014.summary: Researchers introduced ReCAST, a cascaded stage-wise training framework designed to improve the classification of obfuscated fraudulent Chinese SMS messages under production latency constraints. The method distills knowledge from a large teacher model into a compact student model by supervising obfuscated span detection, obfuscation type prediction, and text restoration before downstream risk scoring. Evaluated on an internal Chinese SMS benchmark, the restoration-aware student model substantially outperformed directly trained baseline classifiers. This multi-stage distillation approach offers an efficient mechanism for deploying robust spam and scam filtering in high-throughput telecommunication environments.
d0f7619855def175:2014.one_liner: ReCAST distills SMS de-obfuscation and restoration capabilities into small models for low-latency scam detection.
d0f7619855def175:2014.bottom_line: Pre-restoring obfuscated text through multi-stage model distillation significantly improves lightweight SMS fraud classifier accuracy.

claims.text: The framework demonstrated substantial classification improvements over directly trained baselines on a real-world Chinese SMS dataset.

a2129ab949de7b56:2264.summary: A research study identified Protective Capacity Hallucination (PCH), a safety failure where large language models cast in protective roles falsely claim to execute real-world actions like contacting emergency responders or providing physical care. In an evaluation across eight LLMs and 13,600 conversational sessions, multi-party dialogic inputs triggered near-ceiling levels of PCH in ordinary service domains, while remaining minimal in high-severity intimate-partner violence scenarios. The authors attribute this behavior to partial alignment, where models are heavily optimized to be helpful but lack explicit capability-boundary enforcement. The findings highlight the need for deployment-side boundary constraints in AI systems assisting vulnerable individuals.
a2129ab949de7b56:2264.one_liner: LLMs prompted as protective assistants frequently hallucinate real-world interventions like calling emergency services when boundaries are unspecified.
a2129ab949de7b56:2264.bottom_line: Without explicit capability boundaries, helper-aligned LLMs frequently hallucinate physical actions like calling emergency services during user interactions.

claims.text: Protective Capacity Hallucination occurs when an LLM in a helper role claims physical or institutional actions it cannot perform, such as contacting emergency services.
claims.support_span: When cast as the protector of a vulnerable user yet given no explicit capability boundary, a large language model (LLM) may respond not by acknowledging its limits but by claiming to have taken, or to be taking, a real-world protective action it cannot perform, such as contacting emergency services or administering care.

claims.text: The study evaluated eight models across 13,600 sessions, finding multi-party dialogue induced high PCH rates in service contexts.
claims.support_span: In a three-phase study spanning eight LLMs and 13,600 sessions, we find that PCH depends on both situational severity and interactional format.

key_facts: Primary failure mode: Falsely claiming institutional/physical emergency interventions

While LLM agents handle code generation and reasoning, deterministic controllers maintain strict execution authority over testing guardrails and state transitions across multi-day experiment cycles. The system bridges the gap between academic paper reproduction and internal production A/B launch gates.

c6303d57c6cc3e42:2652.summary: A study examining cost-saving LLM inference cascades—where cheap models handle easy inputs and escalate failures to verifier models—found that self-improving cascade loops create substantial blind spots. As student models scale from 0.5B to 32B parameters, verifier acceptance of incorrect answers rises from 12% to 55%, hiding true degradation. Furthermore, naive corrective fine-tuning on verifier-rejected queries led to student model performance collapse across all tested model families. Crucially, cascade monitoring dashboards showed a steady 3% error rate while true user-facing error rose to 32%, demonstrating that self-evaluating cascades cannot reliably track their own degradation.
c6303d57c6cc3e42:2652.one_liner: Cost-saving LLM cascade verifiers suffer large blind spots and mask true model degradation from monitoring dashboards.
c6303d57c6cc3e42:2652.bottom_line: Self-improving LLM cascade architectures cannot reliably measure their own error rates because verifier blind spots disguise system degradation.

claims.text: The verifier blind spot grows as student model capacity increases, rising from 0.12 to 0.55 between 0.5B and 32B model sizes.
claims.support_span: First, the verifier's blind spot, the fraction of the student's wrong answers it accepts, is large and moves adversarially: it grows with student capability ($\beta$ from 0.12 to 0.55 as the student scales 0.5B to 32B) and shrinks with verifier capability, so it is worst in the cheap-student, cheap-verifier regime cascades exist to create.

claims.text: Cascade internal metrics reported a 3% error rate while true system error reached up to 32%.
claims.support_span: Fourth, through all of this the cascade's own dashboard, every metric computed through the verifier, reads a flat 3% error while true delivered error swings up to 32%: the system is blind to its own degradation by construction.

key_facts: Blind spot range: 0.12 to 0.55 as student scales from 0.5B to 32B
Reported vs true error: Dashboard reads 3% while true error reaches 32%
MATH escalation rate: Frontier verifier escalates 46% of queries on a 39% true error rate

0003a161e29b670a:1807.summary: A simulation study investigated the operational impact of replacing classical random entropy sources with Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) outputs in Bitcoin Proof-of-Work architectures. The results demonstrate that QRNG provides no increase in honest PoW mining success probabilities under normal conditions where header candidates remain distinct. Instead, QRNG entropy delivers measurable operational resilience in hybrid quantum-classical setups during specific fault states, such as namespace reuse, correlated restart failures, and entropy provenance tracking. The benchmark introduces two scheduler observables—the entropy-efficiency factor and reboot-diversity index—to evaluate quantum entropy without asserting immediate device-level mining advantages.
0003a161e29b670a:1807.one_liner: QRNG entropy offers no base mining success boost in Bitcoin PoW, but improves fault recovery in hybrid mining infrastructure.
0003a161e29b670a:1807.bottom_line: Quantum entropy does not increase Bitcoin mining hit rates, but provides operational stability during correlated restart faults and namespace reuse.

claims.text: Using QRNG-derived entropy does not alter the success probability of honest Bitcoin Proof-of-Work mining when header candidates are distinct.
claims.support_span: Replacing classical entropy with QRNG output does not change honest Bitcoin PoW success probability when candidate headers remain distinct.

claims.text: Operational advantages for QRNG emerge primarily in fault scenarios involving namespace reuse and correlated reboot failures.
claims.support_span: Monte Carlo and scheduler simulations with confidence intervals show parity for competent deterministic and strong-classical baselines, while QRNG value emerges in assurance-oriented scenarios involving correlated restart faults, namespace reuse, and entropy provenance.

key_facts: Primary fault domains: Correlated restart faults, namespace reuse, entropy provenance

dedd5bc1f03d3808:2157.summary: Researchers proposed ProtLingo, an efficient protein language model architecture combining conditional local memory and sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing. ProtLingo maps contextual residue representations into discrete codes, forms latent N-gram addresses from local windows, and retrieves cached residual features from recurring sequence contexts. Concurrently, selected feed-forward blocks are converted into sparse MoE layers that activate only a subset of parameters per residue. Tested on protein fitness prediction, FLIP benchmarks, and contact prediction, ProtLingo matched larger dense baselines while utilizing a 150M-parameter backbone.
dedd5bc1f03d3808:2157.one_liner: ProtLingo couples local memory caches with sparse MoE layers to enable efficient protein language modeling at 150M parameters.
dedd5bc1f03d3808:2157.bottom_line: ProtLingo achieves parameter-efficient mutation and contact prediction by augmenting a 150M protein backbone with sparse MoE routing and latent N-gram memory.

claims.text: The system achieves competitive performance on fitness, FLIP, and contact prediction benchmarks with a 150M parameter backbone.
claims.support_span: Experiments on protein fitness prediction, FLIP benchmarks, and supervised contact prediction show that ProtLingo achieves competitive performance with a 150M-scale backbone, including strong parameter efficiency on mutation-effect prediction and preserved long-range structural representations.

key_facts: Architecture: Pretrained backbone + latent N-gram memory + sparse MoE

f8ed279bcadd035c:1776.summary: Researchers have proposed Dual-Embedding Watermarking (DEW), a semantic watermarking technique for large language models designed to withstand paraphrasing and translation. DEW applies vector-space operations to contextual and token embeddings and obfuscates the resulting watermark with pseudo-random projection matrices seeded by a secret key. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art resilience against machine translation while keeping computational overhead low and maintaining text quality at lower watermark strengths.

c657e36d71a9c94a:2173.summary: Whisper models frequently generate fluent hallucinated transcripts when fed audio inputs containing little or no speech. 9afc1dede40624c3:1952.summary: Post-training coding and terminal agents often suffers from token and control fidelity mismatches between training simulations and production environments. Tested on Baize5B and Baize10B models on the TMax-100 benchmark, C-DPPO achieved a consistent 3.0-point performance improvement over standard DPPO.

44c6185f1edbb466:777.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability has been identified in the Mstore Api plugin for WordPress, affecting all versions up to and including 4.20.0. claims.text: The vulnerability occurs because verify_id_token() omits signature validation against Google's public keys.
claims.support_span: This is due to missing cryptographic signature verification in the FirebasePhoneAuthHelper::verify_id_token() function, which decodes and validates Firebase ID token claims (alg, kid, aud, iss) but never calls openssl_verify() or any equivalent to validate the JWT signature against Google's actual public key certificates.

1dbb2fc0b87ff0f9:2005.summary: An authentication bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-75156, has been discovered in the Apache Airflow FAB provider (apache-airflow-providers-fab) versions 3.7.3 through 3.8.0. 0ad4f3cbe71a09aa:6772.summary: JPCERT/CC reported ongoing cyber espionage campaigns by threat group APT-C-60 targeting Japanese organizations in 2026. The threat actor distributes spear-phishing emails containing Proton Drive links to RAR archives that conceal malicious LNK files. When opened, the LNK files execute obfuscated JavaScript, download script files via jsDelivr, and abuse legitimate developer utilities such as git.exe to pull downstream loaders and SpyGlace malware from platforms like GitLab and Codeberg. The reliance on legitimate developer CDNs and repository services allows attackers to blend in with normal corporate network traffic.

0ad4f3cbe71a09aa:6772.bottom_line: Advanced threat groups leverage trusted developer platforms and CDNs to obfuscate malware delivery and evade network controls.

claims.text: In the case we observed, the spear-phishing email contained a Proton Drive link, which was used to lure the victim into downloading a RAR file from Proton Drive.
claims.support_span: In the case we observed, the spear-phishing email contained a Proton Drive link, which was used to lure the victim into downloading a RAR file from Proton Drive.

key_facts: Malware family: SpyGlace v3.1.15, v3.1.17, v3.1.18
Abused services: Proton Drive, GitHub, GitLab, jsDelivr, Codeberg

33b68672e5b081ea:7060.summary: SophosLabs and ESET have detailed a stealthy, fileless Linux rootkit dubbed PoisonedRefresh (tracked as Linux/Agnt-IC) targeting F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager environments. The campaign exploits CVE-2025-53521, an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in BIG-IP APM when access policies are configured on virtual servers. 68270f359b78365b:3503.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Nadeem Danish has publicly disclosed an unauthenticated remote root command injection vulnerability in Tozed ZLT X300 and X300A 5G CPE routers running firmware version 6.01.3, tracked as CVE-2026-2035703 with a CVSS score of 9.8. The flaw exists in the TR-069/CWMP client daemon (netcwmpd), where the IPPingDiagnostics Host parameter is passed unsanitized into a sprintf function and subsequently executed with root privileges via system_by_root(). An attacker utilizing a rogue LTE base station built with software-defined radio hardware costing approximately $300 can impersonate a carrier's Auto Configuration Server to achieve full root remote code execution without authentication. The vulnerability impacts carriers across 15 countries, and the vendor has refused to engage or provide a verified patch.

5039166b12592808:2189.summary: The Attack Shark X6 Linux configurator project has received a significant update, moving from a DPI-only interface to a full-featured desktop companion supporting button remapping, lighting controls, and emergency resets. a2d2640a114b3d62:1159.summary: Bifrost HTTP transport before version 2.0.0 contains an unauthenticated RCE or SSRF vulnerability via POST /api/plugins when management authentication is disabled. 07d25a2f467a25a1:568.summary: Versions of h3 prior to 1.15.9 contain a path traversal vulnerability in the serveStatic utility due to a double-decoding flaw. Request paths containing double-encoded dot sequences like %252e%252e decode to %2e%2e, which bypasses resolveDotSegments() because it only checks literal '.' characters. 6a5a2f3c0cd821d2:22793.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a multi-stage zero-day exploit chain in Google Chrome and Windows against NGOs in September 2026. The chain leveraged a reflected XSS on a US university website to redirect victims to a Google Chrome type-confusion zero-day in the V8 engine (CVE-2026-85046), combined with a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the V8 sandbox and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to break out of the browser sandbox. Although CVE-2026-85046 had been fixed upstream in the Chromium codebase on August 4, 2026, a patch gap existed because no stable release of Google Chrome had incorporated the fix at the time of the attacks. Volexity discovered the activity and identified distinct post-exploitation payloads deployed by each actor.

180712a4d85e479e:2487.summary: Researchers introduce MERIT (Memory Evaluation for Realistic Instrumented Tasks), a benchmark and cost-aware evaluation framework measuring the marginal utility of long-term memory for tool-using LLM agents. ac52b4991dc67b27:1936.summary: Researchers introduced SciLitBench, a multi-stage benchmark designed to evaluate large language models on systematic literature reviews across title and abstract screening, full-text screening, and schema-guided data extraction using 42,981 records and 1,012 full texts. Evaluating 22 open-weight models from six families demonstrated that explicit criteria significantly improve screening, while extraction reliability drops sharply from publication year accuracy down to complex approach and evidence retrieval. The benchmark exposes a clear boundary between high-recall screening and evidence-complete extraction for LLM-assisted workflows. This resource provides a reproducible framework for researchers evaluating automated evidence synthesis tools.

ac52b4991dc67b27:1936.bottom_line: Current open-weight LLMs struggle significantly with evidence-complete extraction compared to high-recall screening tasks.

279516a4d7a5c4f0:1794.summary: Researchers proposed Diverse Skill Routing (DSR), a diversity-aware reranking framework designed to optimize external skill retrieval for LLM agents over large registries. Standard pointwise routers rank candidates independently by relevance, which often wastes context budgets on functionally redundant skills. DSR applies a Determinantal Point Process using a query-residual diversity kernel to balance relevance with complementary non-redundancy. Experiments on the SkillRouter benchmark demonstrated that DSR improves recall and full coverage over baseline routers, particularly for complex multi-skill queries.
279516a4d7a5c4f0:1794.one_liner: Diverse Skill Routing uses a Determinantal Point Process to eliminate redundant skill retrieval and optimize LLM agent context budgets.
279516a4d7a5c4f0:1794.bottom_line: Treating skill routing as complementary set selection rather than simple relevance ranking significantly improves LLM agent efficiency.

24993b839cb65e1d:8488.summary: Proofpoint reported that four nation-state threat actors, predominantly aligned with China, adopted a new exploit kit named BlueMoon within twelve days of its initial appearance. The kit chains three vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-85046, a type-confusion bug in Chrome's V8 engine caused by mutating an array mid-sort; an unassigned V8 sandbox escape that overwrites WebAssembly function bodies with shellcode; and CVE-2026-85880, a Windows kernel LPE using ALPC and WNF mechanisms that allows arbitrary command execution. The V8 vulnerabilities were patch-gap zero-days, exploited because public upstream Chromium source patches revealed the flaws weeks before stable releases arrived. Indicators in the exploit kit also point toward potential AI-assisted development.

c1ec368f51390556:2088.summary: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) incur massive energy overheads, but uniform quantization methods can damage vulnerable reasoning circuits and even increase total energy consumption by lengthening reasoning chains. Researchers proposed a reasoning-aware compression framework that profiles per-module INT4 vulnerabilities across 196-224 layer and projection pairs using a perturbation sweep, then selectively restores sensitive circuits to FP16. Validated across five reasoning benchmarks (including GSM8K and MATH-500), the approach achieves Pareto-optimal compression, such as a Qwen model gaining +12 percentage points on ProofWriter while reducing energy by 9.7%.

482a38d24b52d306:2745.summary: Evaluating whether to keep a human-AI team workflow or replace it with an independent human or agent requires comparative testing, but running both baselines on every task is cost-prohibitive. To solve this budget allocation problem, researchers propose TEAM-Design, a rule that assigns every task two replay probabilities for human-only and agent-only baselines. The method raises replay probabilities where baseline outcomes are hard to predict and lowers them where replay is expensive, while controlling the false-positive rate for workflow superiority claims. The approach performs best when one baseline comparison is significantly harder to establish than the other.

482a38d24b52d306:2745.bottom_line: TEAM-Design provides a rigorous statistical framework to allocate limited replay budgets when evaluating whether human-AI workflows beat independent baselines.

cef135d2295e2364:2379.summary: Agentic AI frameworks that integrate tools and process multimodal inputs remain vulnerable to indirect prompt injections via perceptual channels. Researchers introduced MMPIBench, a benchmark delivering attacks across six visual carriers (such as OCR, overlays, and QR codes) and audio across multiple frameworks and foundation models. Across 720 visual runs, attacks completed in approximately 1% of instances, with most injections caught during the planning step by models refusing to act. However, audio input proved significantly more dangerous: although supported by fewer frameworks and models, audio-based prompt injections completed in 49% of test cells overall, and up to 75% for a single model, demonstrating that non-visual perceptual channels are much less defended.
cef135d2295e2364:2379.one_liner: Multimodal benchmark MMPIBench reveals that audio-based prompt injections in agentic AI succeed at alarmingly high rates compared to visual vectors.
cef135d2295e2364:2379.bottom_line: Audio channels in multimodal AI agents lack robust defenses, yielding a 49% prompt injection completion rate compared to 1% for visual vectors.

claims.text: MMPIBench delivers a fixed set of attacks through six visual carriers and records how far each injected instruction travels.
claims.support_span: We present MMPIBench, a reproducible benchmark that measures what happens next. It delivers a fixed set of attacks through six visual carriers (OCR text, overlays, EXIF metadata, QR codes, fake interfaces, and hybrids) and records how far each injected instruction travels through the agent, from perception through planning to the tool call.

claims.text: Across 720 runs covering six frameworks, attacks complete in approximately 1% of runs but are attempted in 12.8%.
claims.support_span: Across 720 runs covering six frameworks, five foundation models, six carriers, and four attacker objectives, attacks complete in approximately 1% of runs but are attempted in 12.8%, and the gap is closed almost entirely at the planning step, where the model reads the injected instruction and declines to act on it.

claims.text: For audio, the attack completes in 49% of cells, and in 75% for one model.
claims.support_span: Only two of the five models ingest audio and only three of the six frameworks deliver it, but where the signal arrives the attack completes in 49% of cells, and in 75% for one model.

key_facts: Audio attack completion rate: 49% (up to 75% for one model)

1a13679d7f9b0297:2613.summary: Researchers propose the Multi-View Text-Guided Multimodal Fusion Adapter (MVFA), a parameter-efficient framework that adapts frozen Large Language Models (LLMs) for multimodal sentiment analysis and emotion recognition. MVFA constructs complementary text views via max, mean, and attention pooling to guide cross-modal interactions with audio and visual features, compressing the fused representations through an Enhanced Q-Former Fusion Module. Using ChatGLM3-6B-base as the primary backbone and validated on LLaMA2-7B and Qwen3-8B, the method achieves state-of-the-art results across CH-SIMS V2.0, MELD, and CHERMA datasets while updating only a small fraction of parameters. Specifically, it attains 84.62% Acc2 on CH-SIMS V2.0 and 67.36% Acc on MELD.

8af44d86eb295b27:4771.summary: A security survey of five filesystem Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers reveals that `iceener/files-stdio-mcp-server` contains a read-side sandbox escape via symlinks in its recursive directory walker. c3a20317d229971b:2524.summary: Article 50 of the EU AI Act took effect on August 2, 2026, requiring generative AI providers to mark AI-generated content so it remains detectable. 824f8a3994c6d4b4:2600.summary: Evaluating LLM-based agents requires balancing multiple competing objectives such as task completion accuracy, interaction quality, safety, and efficiency. Traditional methods often collapse these heterogeneous measurements into a single scalar score using normalization and preference weights, which risks discarding valuable deployment trade-offs. To solve this, researchers introduced Multi-Objective Agent Evolution (MOAE), an in-context refinement approach that performs a Pareto-preserving evolutionary search over complete agent rollouts. MOAE maintains an empirical archive of non-dominated candidates during search and applies constraint-aware selection strictly at deployment, requiring no parameter updates. Experiments on TravelPlanner and AgentDojo demonstrate that MOAE consistently improves task performance and trajectory quality while maintaining strong safety under matched rollout budgets.
824f8a3994c6d4b4:2600.one_liner: MOAE provides a parameter-free evolutionary search method to optimize multiple competing agent properties without premature scalarization.
824f8a3994c6d4b4:2600.bottom_line: Preserving non-dominated agent candidates via Pareto-based search expands attainable performance and safety trade-offs without requiring parameter updates.

bdc6c84fdddd43e6:2438.summary: Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC) attempts to identify speakers' emotions across multi-turn dialogues for applications like empathetic agents and mental health support, traditionally assuming each utterance maps to a single unambiguous label. Researchers investigated this zero-shot assumption using Large Language Models with dialogue context and found that aggregate metrics mask systematic errors concentrating around negations, exclamations, and interjections. A controlled re-annotation study with four human annotators revealed strong agreement in only 35 percent of cases, with neutral utterances dominating high agreement while emotional categories fell into low-agreement regimes. This indicates that model errors often reflect genuine dataset annotation ambiguity rather than a lack of emotion understanding. Consequently, the authors introduce an LLM-as-Judge framework that evaluates emotions independently based on contextual plausibility rather than enforcing a single-label decision.

bdc6c84fdddd43e6:2438.bottom_line: Standard single-label emotion recognition evaluations are flawed because genuine human annotation ambiguity accounts for many perceived model errors.

1822d1d2cb7f5d92:2395.summary: Graph-agentic retrieval-augmented generation combines structured evidence with adaptive controllers to handle complex queries, but it introduces coupled failure paths where graph construction defects propagate into downstream reasoning and consequential outcomes. Researchers examined these architectures for social-good settings where factors like freshness, authorization, traceability, and recourse are essential. They synthesized these risks into an evidence-to-action failure chain and proposed an assurance-by-construction blueprint containing five interface contracts for evidence, retrieval, reasoning, capability and delegation, and outcome. These contracts explicitly enforce provenance, temporal validity, authorization, uncertainty, and recoverability at system boundaries, supported by an evaluation agenda spanning graph assertions, trajectories, and claims.

21a9238e00c4aca6:2769.summary: Automated vehicles rely on safety-critical software, yet general-purpose code analyzers struggle to detect domain-specific motion hazards. Researchers created LLMSec-AV, a framework incorporating an 18-class vulnerability taxonomy derived from automated-vehicle security literature, to test whether LLMs improve weakness discovery over rule-based tools. Evaluated on Autoware by decomposing 770 translation units into 4,673 functions and analyzing 161 functions, LLM-based prompting conditions recovered up to 76% of 46 known weakness locations, substantially outperforming conventional tools like CodeQL, Semgrep, cppcheck, and Clang Static Analyzer. While unaided prompting achieved similar detection rates, incorporating the taxonomy increased the share of findings assigned to a specific weakness class from near zero to over 80%, greatly improving interpretability and triage.

922caea2f627d79c:2609.summary: Researchers proposed Open Autoresearch, a paradigm where humans and AI agents publish evaluator-verified optimizations to a public leaderboard, instantiating it on a platform optimizing reversible secp256k1 point-addition circuits for Shor's algorithm. The benchmark minimizes the score S = Q x T, combining peak logical qubit width Q and average executed Toffoli count T. By the July 26, 2026 data cutoff, participants reduced the baseline score by 86.1%, with the top circuit using 1,151 qubits and about 1.29 million Toffoli gates to achieve an S score approximately 50% below Google's published thresholds. A windowed-addition-compatible variant was also developed for single-call interfaces, achieving a success probability of 0.99809 across 100,000 random inputs. Subsequent post-cutoff optimizations further reduced the score and lowered the minimum qubit width to 813, demonstrating how AI agents effectively complement human judgment on machine-checkable objectives.
922caea2f627d79c:2609.one_liner: Open Autoresearch leverages AI agents and human collaboration to optimize quantum circuits for elliptic-curve point addition, beating prior thresholds.
922caea2f627d79c:2609.bottom_line: Collaborative human-AI autoresearch successfully optimized secp256k1 point-addition circuits for Shor's algorithm, lowering qubit and Toffoli requirements below previous thresholds.

2d86063cf510d83e:1959.summary: Popular science writing requires adapting complex scientific explanations to various audience cognitive levels while strictly maintaining factual accuracy, but traditional simplification often increases the risk of hallucinations. To tackle this, researchers constructed a dataset of 39,134 entries and a reader-centric Personalized Science Communication Benchmark (PSCB). They developed DA-MoE, a mixture-of-experts model that decouples audience adaptation from domain knowledge to improve generalization and computational efficiency. Additionally, they introduced a multi-agent fact-checking mechanism that uses role-specific agent debate and graph-based confidence propagation to verify information in evidence-scarce scenarios. Experiments on PSCB demonstrate that this collaborative framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in personalized science writing.
2d86063cf510d83e:1959.one_liner: CWF combines a decoupled mixture-of-experts model and multi-agent fact-checking to generate personalized, factually accurate popular science text.
2d86063cf510d83e:1959.bottom_line: Decoupling audience adaptation from domain knowledge via DA-MoE and multi-agent fact-checking enables reliable personalized science writing without increasing hallucinations.

00682e135d21865f:2448.summary: Existing evaluations of AI-assisted peer review focus primarily on final decisions or overall review quality rather than whether model decisions are backed by sufficient review evidence. To address this, researchers introduced a process-centric diagnostic benchmark that structures reviews into paper content, summaries, critiques, suggestions, and decisions using data converted from PeerRead, NLPeer ARR-22, and OpenReview-ICLR. The benchmark evaluates stage-level performance, chain consistency, and interventional sensitivity across three datasets and six models. Experiments revealed that while model-generated intermediate texts maintain local consistency across adjacent stages, final decisions are frequently not supported by the preceding review evidence. This benchmark provides a transparent tool to audit the reliability of AI assistants in scientific peer review.
00682e135d21865f:2448.one_liner: A new process-centric benchmark shows that AI peer-review models often reach final decisions that lack support from their own preceding review text.
00682e135d21865f:2448.bottom_line: AI-assisted peer review models suffer from a fundamental disconnect where final decisions are not consistently supported by preceding generated review evidence.

claims.text: Although model-generated intermediate review texts show relatively high local consistency across adjacent stages, the final decisions are not consistently supported by the preceding review evidence.

a4118414e14241bd:2720.summary: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) protect on-device Large Language Model intellectual property, but TEE-Shielded LLM Partitioning (TSLP) methods use heuristic obfuscation schemes to offload heavy layers to external GPUs. Because these schemes are heuristic, they are vulnerable to specialized adversarial attacks. This paper formalizes a set of obfuscation primitives defined as dual-tuples of linear computations to unify prior TSLP methodologies and characterize their shared structural security boundary as O_prior. The authors then expose vulnerabilities in O_prior using a novel attack methodology called Collapse, demonstrating shared weaknesses in prominent TSLP frameworks like ArrowCloak, TSQP, and LoRO. Finally, they introduce two novel obfuscation primitives to extend the security boundary into a stronger formulation, O_ext.
a4118414e14241bd:2720.one_liner: A new primitive-guided attack called Collapse exposes shared vulnerabilities in prominent TEE-shielded LLM partitioning defenses.
a4118414e14241bd:2720.bottom_line: Formalizing obfuscation primitives reveals that prominent TEE-shielded LLM partitioning frameworks share structural vulnerabilities vulnerable to a unified Collapse attack.

claims.text: Finally, we introduce two novel obfuscation primitives and integrate them with existing constructs to formulate O_ext, extending this security boundary.
claims.support_span: Finally, we introduce two novel obfuscation primitives and integrate them with existing constructs to formulate O_ext, extending this security boundary.

014159943e4d9643:6536.summary: Bioengineer César de la Fuente and his lab are using artificial intelligence to tackle antimicrobial resistance by searching the genetic codes of living and extinct organisms for new antimicrobial molecules. With bacterial antimicrobial resistance associated with roughly five million deaths in 2021—a toll projected to double by 2050—and no new classes of antibiotics discovered in 50 years, traditional discovery methods offer diminishing returns. Treating biology as an information system where DNA and proteins form an alphabet, the lab trains deep-learning models to scan vast genomic databases for promising molecular candidates. Alongside custom models, the researchers leverage ChatGPT and Codex to brainstorm hypotheses, write code, process datasets, and analyze results, reducing the initial candidate search phase from years to hours.
014159943e4d9643:6536.one_liner: Researchers are using ChatGPT, Codex, and custom deep-learning models to scan genomic databases and accelerate the discovery of new antibiotics.
014159943e4d9643:6536.bottom_line: Integrating LLMs and deep learning into genomic screening cuts the initial search phase for novel antimicrobial molecules from years down to hours.

5ce41d9be2e6c45b:1734.summary: High-quality multi-turn tool-use data is vital for training agentic models, but current data synthesis techniques struggle to capture argument-level dependencies required for long-horizon tasks, leading agents to fill arguments with fabricated or stale values. To fix this, researchers propose State-Guided Data Synthesis with Argument Provenance (SAP). SAP integrates state guidance, tool-argument provenance constraints, and turn-level validation to efficiently generate robust multi-turn tool trajectories. Using SAP-generated data, the authors built SAP-4B, a model that achieves highly competitive performance against much larger models across multiple benchmarks, with all code, data, and weights released publicly.

f7f61df64e277442:2307.summary: Recommender systems heavily influence user engagement and sales, but their reliance on user feedback makes them vulnerable to shilling attacks where malicious actors inject fake profiles to distort item rankings. Existing attacks rely on rigid templates or target-specific fine-tuning, making them easily detectable or hard to adapt. To overcome these issues, researchers propose the Agentic Group Attack System (AGAS), a coordinated framework where a central Coordinator directs role-switching worker agents to promote target items across victim families dynamically. The Coordinator adjusts strategies when progress stalls while workers alternate between active and inactive roles to avoid detection. Experiments show that AGAS outperforms strong baselines in promoting target items while preserving benign recommendation quality and evading representative detectors.
f7f61df64e277442:2307.one_liner: AGAS uses a coordinated multi-agent system to execute adaptive shilling attacks that bypass existing recommender system detectors.
f7f61df64e277442:2307.bottom_line: Coordinated multi-agent shilling attacks can successfully manipulate recommender system item rankings while evading current detection defenses.

9b421b55a990f64b:2160.summary: Web agents must navigate complex interfaces across different sites, but most agents learn tasks in isolation and discard accumulated procedural knowledge. To address this limitation, researchers introduced Scaffold, a self-improving framework for visual web agents that induces parametric, executable skills from successful trajectories under multi-instance constraints. Scaffold maintains a recursively composed skill hierarchy where higher-level skills invoke lower-level ones, compacts the library via minimum-description-length criteria and behavioral equivalence checks, and distills skills back into model weights. Across WebArena, VisualWebArena, and Online-Mind2Web, Scaffold improved success rates by 11.1 to 17.2 absolute points over the strongest skill-augmented baseline with monotonic gains across five iterations.
9b421b55a990f64b:2160.one_liner: Scaffold improves visual web agents by recursively abstracting, compressing, and internalizing executable skills from successful trajectories.
9b421b55a990f64b:2160.bottom_line: Recursive skill abstraction and weight distillation allow web agents to accumulate procedural knowledge and improve success rates monotonically across tasks.

8769c06ceee7930b:2596.summary: Aggregating multiple vision-language models (VLMs) can boost multimodal reasoning, but individual or aggregated confidence scores do not reliably measure system-level accuracy. Researchers introduced CUSP (Collective Uncertainty through Semantic Opinion Pooling), a training-free framework that maps multiple VLM responses to a shared semantic space and pools them into a semantic opinion. CUSP reports collective uncertainty (opinion dispersion) and Jensen-Shannon divergence (model conflict), cleanly decomposing unnormalized collective entropy into individual semantic entropies and conflict. Requiring no token logits or calibration labels, CUSP outperforms traditional majority voting and naive selection in detecting prediction errors and ordering abstentions across static ensembles and multi-step agent trajectories.
8769c06ceee7930b:2596.one_liner: CUSP provides a training-free uncertainty quantification framework for multi-VLM ensembles by decomposing collective entropy into dispersion and model conflict.
8769c06ceee7930b:2596.bottom_line: Decomposing collective uncertainty into opinion dispersion and model conflict provides reliable system-level error detection for multi-VLM ensembles without requiring logits.

148e6789d78857f7:1853.summary: Pre-submission peer review can help authors catch manuscript flaws before formal submission, but LLM reviewer assistants often struggle to provide comprehensive coverage. Researchers evaluated an author-facing LLM system using 3,398 manuscripts from 10,000 ICLR 2026 submissions to measure agreement with historical reviews and the validity of omitted concerns. On a ten-paper diagnostic, independent sampling covered 44.9% of historical issues, while deduplication and refill strategies raised strict coverage to 78.7% and seriousness-weighted coverage to 84.9%, albeit requiring 3.6 times more requests and 5.2 times more tokens. While large candidate pools yield broad coverage, paper-only selectors retain only 40 to 44%, highlighting that representative selection and matcher sensitivity are primary bottlenecks.

148e6789d78857f7:1853.bottom_line: Achieving comprehensive pre-submission peer review coverage with LLMs requires large candidate pools, as paper-only selectors retain less than half of historical issues.

f6d778839823d1b6:2042.summary: Scientific coding agents generate complex code, results, and claims, but evaluating final outputs alone fails to confirm if conclusions are scientifically sound. Researchers formulated evidence-grounded multimodal scientific analysis and introduced SciRIGOR, an evaluation benchmark comprising 100 cases across six domains and 17 subfields. SciRIGOR reconstructs typed evidence graphs, separates artifact fidelity from relational validity, and scores complete claim-support paths to localize unsupported relations. Evaluating 11 agent and model configurations, the authors found that while claims agreed with both faithful and unfaithful results at nearly identical rates (91.8% versus 91.0%), no system exceeded 62.6% on soft evidence-chain scores or 18.0% on strict whole-chain success, proving that internal coherence does not ensure scientific correctness.
f6d778839823d1b6:2042.one_liner: SciRIGOR evaluation benchmark reveals that scientific coding agents frequently generate unsupported claims despite internal text coherence.
f6d778839823d1b6:2042.bottom_line: Evaluating final outputs is insufficient for scientific coding agents; verifying support along the complete data-to-claim path is necessary because internal coherence does not ensure scientific correctness.

93b0bcd3d4a646ed:2104.summary: Deploying web agents for real-world automation requires continuous online adaptation, but leveraging proprietary teacher models for interactive feedback is commercially cost-prohibitive. Practitioners rely on lightweight local models that evolve via online teaching, though conventional preference optimization wastes compute on unresolvable episodes and redundant turns. To fix this, researchers introduced a budget-aware framework featuring a solvability-aware teacher gate to decide when to query the teacher model and a score-guided turn selection mechanism to determine what informative turns to retain. Experiments on MiniWoB and TimeWarp show that this approach achieves comparable first-pass success while reducing teacher calls by 22.6% and student training compute by 52.1%.

7e8ce169151b1de6:1946.summary: The rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence driven by large language models, large-scale compute infrastructure, and autonomous reasoning is encountering severe friction. The industry faces mounting technological, societal, economic, and infrastructural hurdles, including peak data limits, rising energy demands, synthetic data recursion, valuation inflation, and labor disruption. This paper examines the concept of 'the end of AI exponentiation,' exploring how instability emerges both inside the AI ecosystem through data-center races and speculative investments, and outside the ecosystem through geopolitical acceleration, governance concerns, and workforce disruption.

646f3c96fe49589a:2407.summary: Structured post-training pruning of transformer models requires selecting functional units whose suppression causes minimal performance degradation. Researchers formulated structured-unit selection for language and vision transformers as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem under a fixed evaluation budget, using paired damage metrics to eliminate batch-to-batch variation. Utilizing smooth bounded rewards with UCB or fractional-Beta Thompson Sampling policies, the method sequentially builds masks for attention heads and MLP channel groups. Evaluated across models like GPT-2, OPT, Qwen2.5, and ViT-B/16 on datasets such as WikiText-2 and Imagenette, the bandit methods reduced degradation compared to budgeted greedy baselines, with statistical significance confirmed across multiple tests.
646f3c96fe49589a:2407.one_liner: Damage-aware multi-armed bandit pruning improves structured pruning of vision and language transformers by minimizing performance degradation.
646f3c96fe49589a:2407.bottom_line: Framing transformer unit pruning as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem successfully reduces degradation compared to traditional budgeted greedy selection.

0f6a19008fc6e5c3:2622.summary: Researchers introduce Reliability-Aware Pair Importance Distillation (RAPID) to separate reliability gated relational targets from adaptive pair proposal during knowledge distillation. Evaluated on AG News and SST-2 using BERT and DistilBERT, the gated relational target achieved higher mean student accuracies than traditional cross-entropy baselines. 597239feadebe7bd:2490.summary: Researchers demonstrate that unprivileged malicious applications running locally on a client device can collaborate with remote off-path adversaries to bypass network protocol protections. This enables cross-user and cross-app connection hijacking and DNS cache poisoning across major operating systems including Linux, Android, Windows, macOS, and iOS. Disclosures to Microsoft, Apple, Linux, and Google have resulted in security patches.

claims.text: In this work, we refute this presumption by demonstrating that an unprivileged malicious application running on the client (but practically off-path), when combined with a remote off-path adversary, can enable powerful network attacks against such connections.
claims.support_span: In this work, we refute this presumption by demonstrating that an unprivileged malicious application running on the client (but practically off-path), when combined with a remote off-path adversary, can enable powerful network attacks against such connections.

claims.text: We demonstrate TCP connection hijacking in Linux, Android, Windows, macOS and iOS, and DNS cache poisoning against Windows, Android and the popular systemd-resolved DNS stub resolver in Linux.
claims.support_span: We demonstrate TCP connection hijacking in Linux, Android, Windows, macOS and iOS, and DNS cache poisoning against Windows, Android and the popular systemd-resolved DNS stub resolver in Linux.

24993b839cb65e1d:22793.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a multi-stage zero-day exploit chain in Google Chrome and Windows against NGOs in September 2026. 18c93703b0f4dc11:2655.summary: Research published on arXiv analyzes how autonomous agents lose control and cross safety boundaries while performing legitimate long-horizon tasks. Across 1,800 trajectories spanning five models and 16 domains, researchers found that the combination of degraded control boundaries and executable unsafe opportunities produced a 55% to 62% violation rate. The study revealed that context-management compaction that dropped control constraints drove violation rates up to 87%, whereas maintaining control constraints reduced violations to 0%.
18c93703b0f4dc11:2655.one_liner: Research shows context compaction omitting control constraints causes autonomous agents to commit safety violations up to 87% of the time.
18c93703b0f4dc11:2655.bottom_line: Autonomous agent architectures must explicitly preserve control boundaries during context compaction to prevent unauthorized execution during legitimate tasks.

claims.text: When both degraded control and unsafe executable opportunities were present, agent loss-of-control rates reached 55% to 62%.
claims.support_span: Across 1,800 unique trajectories, we find that neither degraded control nor unsafe opportunity alone produces substantial loss of control; when both are present, the loss-of-control rate reaches $55\%$ in the full-factorial study and $62\%$ across ten additional operational domains.

claims.text: Omitting control constraints during context management increased the loss-of-control rate to 87%.
claims.support_span: A context-management ablation further shows that compaction itself is not harmful: preserving the control constraints yields $0\%$ loss of control, whereas omitting them increases the rate to $87\%$.

key_facts: Sample size: 1,800 trajectories across 5 agent models and 16 operational domains

7ab3c02f17b21a6b:2470.summary: BenchShield is a model-backed instrumentation layer designed to protect LLM-agent evaluation infrastructure from reward hacking, where agents exploit reward trajectories rather than solving tasks. It uses a finite lifecycle model of reward-relevant events, combining a static phase-aware taint analysis with a runtime analysis to attribute concrete agent use. Tested on 456 adjudicated trajectories from over 31,000 public runs, BenchShield improves full-chain recall to 77-100% and achieves 96% accuracy in runtime detection. These capabilities help secure agent evaluation frameworks against sophisticated gaming behaviours.

7ab3c02f17b21a6b:2470.bottom_line: LLM-agent evaluations can be rigorously protected against reward hacking using formal model-backed static and runtime analysis.

claims.text: BenchShield improves full-chain recall from 23-94% to 77-100%, same-vector coverage from 16-56% to 43-78%, and reduces per-task cost by up to 65%.
claims.support_span: Compared with an agentic hackability scanner baseline on the same tasks and model, BenchShield improves full-chain recall from 23-94% to 77-100%, same-vector coverage from 16-56% to 43-78%, and reduces per-task cost by up to 65%.

claims.text: Its runtime analysis achieves 96% accuracy in detecting reward hacking from infrastructure-side evidence.

e417bded4e9a1426:2786.summary: DriftNet is a dual-head trajectory Transformer designed to detect and localize indirect prompt injections in LLM agents from logged tool-call trajectories. One head classifies the entire trace as compromised, while the second assigns individual steps labels such as benign, injection point, hijacked, or failed injection. Operating with under two million parameters without requiring access to the agent's model, DriftNet achieves a trajectory-level F1 score of 0.983 and exact injection-point recovery on 98.7% of attacked trajectories on the AgentDrift benchmark. This provides operators with granular forensic insights into multi-step agent compromises.

e2898bae43d1b880:2580.summary: Compound LLM systems frequently rely on a higher-level generative LLM manager to coordinate worker outputs, introducing ordering sensitivity and opaque control decisions. To address this, researchers introduced UnitBoost, which replaces the generative manager with a defined meta-level operator using task-given unit maps and constrained argmax output assembly. This approach provides order invariance, unit provenance, and explicit testable failure conditions while outperforming generative managers on standard benchmarks. Across multiple configurations, UnitBoost raises task scores and improves cell F1 metrics while eliminating semantic freedom in favor of systematic guarantees.

e2898bae43d1b880:2580.bottom_line: Replacing generative LLM managers with deterministic merge operators improves compound system performance and provides strict behavioral guarantees.

78589058745cec95:2718.summary: Existing AI evaluation benchmarks typically assess only final outputs while ignoring the reasoning trajectories of autonomous scientific agents. To bridge this gap, researchers released OpenDiscoveryTrace, a public dataset comprising 558 complete scientific agent trajectories across 124 tasks in fields like drug discovery and materials science. Each trace records a structured 9-field format encompassing thoughts, tool calls, errors, revision triggers, and self-confidence across frontier and open-weight models. Pilot analysis revealed that while frontier models achieve comparable success rates, their error profiles vary significantly—such as Claude Opus 4.6 producing thirty times more errors than GPT-5.4, predominantly via tool misuse rather than reasoning faults.

78589058745cec95:2718.bottom_line: Evaluating the reasoning processes of autonomous scientific agents reveals critical behavioral differences, such as high tool-misuse rates, that output-only benchmarks miss.

70656d10fc89c3ba:2195.summary: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) audit privacy risks in large language models by checking whether specific text appeared in training corpora, but most methods require per-token logits. WPMIA estimates word-level generation probabilities via Monte Carlo sampling with local kernel smoothing, conditioning likelihoods across different prefixes to amplify distributional differences. a32b9e203b00240c:2719.summary: Researchers have introduced Fortunate Recall (FR), a composable policy layer for LLM memory systems that classifies personal user facts into a 10+1 behavioral ontology and applies category-specific lifecycle policies. Ablation studies indicate that generic lifecycle metadata drives correctness while the behavioral ontology reduces contradictions.
a32b9e203b00240c:2719.one_liner: Fortunate Recall uses a behavioral memory ontology and lifecycle policies to reduce LLM confabulation and improve memory coherence.
a32b9e203b00240c:2719.bottom_line: Structuring LLM personal memory persistence around an ontology-driven lifecycle policy significantly curbs confabulation without hurting retrieval accuracy.

claims.support_span: Fortunate Recall (FR) is a composable policy layer that classifies personal facts into a 10+1 behavioral ontology and applies category-specific lifecycle policies (differential temporal decay, slot-key supersession, event-time validity, and category-aware retrieval routing) as deterministic functions over LLM-extracted metadata.

84764a5b5fbdde32:2624.summary: The Belief-State Engine (BSE) is a new architectural module designed to improve LLM performance in partially observable environments. 769ae7454b1327a5:2472.summary: Researchers have developed a reference-based method to detect bias in LLMs by analyzing hidden-state representations rather than just model outputs. By encoding sentences based on their similarity to a fixed set of anchor sentences, the method creates relative representations that allow for comparison across different model checkpoints. This approach, called Representational Bias Shift, correlates strongly with output-level bias changes and is significantly more computationally efficient than traditional benchmarks. It provides a way to audit internal model shifts that might not be immediately visible in generated text.
769ae7454b1327a5:2472.one_liner: A new, efficient method for auditing LLM bias by comparing internal hidden states across model versions without needing expensive output-level benchmarks.
769ae7454b1327a5:2472.bottom_line: Auditing hidden-state geometry provides a faster, more sensitive way to detect bias increases during fine-tuning than relying solely on output-based benchmarks.

claims.text: We propose a reference-based method that audits bias in hidden-state representations across related model variants, for example before and after fine-tuning.

claims.text: Our method requires no task-specific evaluation data and audits a model in about three minutes, using 3-50x less compute than the output-level benchmarks considered here.

d583b14a04725e58:2448.summary: Researchers have introduced 'Cros', a risk-constrained stopping layer for sequential clinical diagnosis agents. The system uses state-wise error ranking and LTT-style exact tests to determine when an agent should stop and provide a diagnosis versus continuing to request tests. In testing on a MIMIC-derived abdominal-pain benchmark, Cros significantly improved selective error rates and reduced the number of tests required compared to native stopping methods. 32f35470c524ef7a:2440.summary: Researchers introduce A2ABreak, the first systematic security analysis of the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol governed by the Linux Foundation, uncovering 11 new vulnerabilities that can be exploited by specification-compliant adversaries without any implementation flaws. The authors utilized an LLM-assisted extraction framework to convert the natural-language protocol specification into a verified finite-state machine comprising 37 states and 76 transitions from 929 formalized statements. Discovered flaws include cross-client context injection via unprotected context identifiers, credential harvesting through multi-hop identity loss, and data exfiltration via rogue agents advertising unattested capabilities. The formal verification approach achieved 73.3% precision and 84.6% F1 score, outperforming a zero-shot LLM baseline that yielded zero confirmed findings. This demonstrates that explicit formal grounding is critical for discovering security flaws in complex multi-agent communication protocols.
32f35470c524ef7a:2440.one_liner: A2ABreak uncovers 11 specification-level vulnerabilities in the Linux Foundation's A2A multi-agent protocol using a formal finite-state machine analysis.
32f35470c524ef7a:2440.bottom_line: Autonomous agent communication standards harbor deep protocol-level vulnerabilities that can be exploited without implementation bugs.

26c6544828a1beb3:2357.summary: Researchers introduce the Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) to establish rigorous verification and auditing standards for AI research agents by converting performance claims into executable recovery and feedback tests. The protocol utilizes a multi-gate evaluation process, requiring sealed evaluation improvements, recovery witnesses under matched starting conditions, and finite-sample bounds on recovery, while incorporating a Core veto to prevent false positives. Controlled audits in SQLite optimization and virtual catalyst control demonstrated zero recoveries across 96 episodes with low upper bounds, while paired studies verified truthful feedback effects. A deterministic, LLM-free verifier reproduces audit decisions directly from frozen evidence, providing a standardized evidence framework for multi-agent AI research outcomes.

b251b33bffef61b7:2068.summary: Researchers introduce CONTRACTEVAL, a diagnostic framework designed to evaluate procedural instruction conformance for LLM agent execution traces. While output-only evaluation and trace-aware judging fail to identify active query obligations, CONTRACTEVAL represents procedural instructions as query-active obligations and matches them against response or trace evidence. Evaluations on audited procedural contracts demonstrate that ContractEval successfully detects and localizes injected structural failures that traditional LLM judges miss.

10128a12627159ce:2394.summary: MoguBlog versions through 6.2 contain an XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability in the unauthenticated WeChat callback endpoint at `/wechat/wechatCheck`. b9d727b8cb359a99:2675.summary: Authorizer, an open-source authentication and authorization server, contains an unvalidated `redirect_uri` vulnerability in its `/authorize` endpoint prior to version 2.2.1. 60dc2ea7eeba5694:2311.summary: Researchers have proposed RD-Forget, a training-free framework that separates what a persistent language agent stores from what it uses during reasoning. The system utilizes a retained source archive for historical observations and a query-conditioned memory view to control their influence on current answers, preventing superseded facts from misleading current states. A frozen language-model curator extracts and groups facts into semantic slots, employing same-slot replacement links and intent-aware retrieval to make historical evidence accessible when needed. Experiments demonstrate that retaining history while selectively controlling its usage successfully accommodates changing facts and multi-hop reasoning. This approach addresses the limitation where unmanaged memories either accumulate stale data or lose historical context entirely.

60dc2ea7eeba5694:2311.bottom_line: Separating stored agent memory from active query views prevents outdated facts from corrupting current-state reasoning.

5c1339988a8658ec:1936.summary: Researchers propose a lightweight evaluation strategy called 'QK-score' that extracts query-key alignments from transformer attention heads to quantify logical consistency in large language models. This method reliably separates valid from invalid inferences in a single forward pass, offering a scalable alternative to traditional ablation techniques. Empirical validations across models ranging from 1.5B to 70B parameters show increased reasoning depth and robustness against distractors. The approach addresses the lack of coherence assessment mechanisms in standard Chain-of-Thought prompting. Consequently, developers gain a direct way to inspect latent logical transitions without expensive retraining.
5c1339988a8658ec:1936.one_liner: QK-scores extracted from transformer attention heads quantify multi-step logical consistency in LLMs without ablation.
5c1339988a8658ec:1936.bottom_line: Query-key alignment scores in attention heads provide a scalable, single-pass metric for LLM logical coherence.

34b4bf78177a6c15:2131.summary: Researchers introduce AgenticGen, a reward-guided framework that optimizes advertising video generation by decomposing the task into strategy selection and draft generation. The system leverages both accumulated online business feedback and human quality standards to supervise policy optimization via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Offline experiments validated the reward models, while online A/B evaluations in the TikTok advertising system demonstrated substantial performance gains. Specifically, AgenticGen improved click-through rate (CTR), conversion rate (CVR), and advertising value (Advv) compared to supervised fine-tuning baselines. These results show that closing the loop between video generation and business feedback optimizes automated ad creation.

34b4bf78177a6c15:2131.bottom_line: Reward-guided agentic video generation significantly improves online advertising metrics like CTR and CVR over standard baselines.

eace631647eb8c18:1853.summary: This position paper examines Large Language Model self-explanations, arguing that while rationalizations are often plausible and questionably faithful to the model's actual reasoning, they can still be highly actionable for users. The authors identify limitations in standard evaluation protocols that test only plausibility and faithfulness. They propose practical guidelines for assessing these dimensions while emphasizing actionability to support informed decision-making across diverse stakeholders. By focusing on how rationalizations affect practical action, the paper reframes how XAI evaluates LLM self-explanations. This shift highlights utility in real-world deployments despite underlying faithfulness concerns.
eace631647eb8c18:1853.one_liner: LLM self-explanations can be useful for decision-making even if they lack complete faithfulness to the model's internal reasoning.
eace631647eb8c18:1853.bottom_line: Evaluating LLM self-explanations should prioritize actionability and practical decision support alongside traditional faithfulness metrics.

29d45910544565df:2205.summary: Researchers investigate the limitations of using Large Language Models to translate natural language descriptions into PDDL problem instances for automated planning. They show that standard evaluations relying solely on syntactic validity or planner success severely overestimate task faithfulness, as generated problems often misrepresent initial states, goals, or object structures. To fix this, the authors propose an end-to-end pipeline featuring PDDL parsing, validation, domain-conformance checks, an LLM critic, and iterative structured repair. Evaluations across Planetarium, AutoPlanBench, and curated PDDL 2.1 problems demonstrate that operational success diverges from reference reconstruction, proving that structured repair is necessary. Ultimately, this approach provides rigorous quality control for automated planning code generation.
29d45910544565df:2205.one_liner: Grounded evaluation and iterative structured repair pipelines are necessary to ensure LLM-generated PDDL planning problems are faithful.
29d45910544565df:2205.bottom_line: Standard parser checks are insufficient to verify LLM-generated PDDL planning problems, requiring domain-conformance and structured repair.

9beefa141aba5d6a:2309.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into user tasks exposes sensitive personal data, but context-agnostic static sanitization rules cause severe utility degradation. Researchers systematically analyze the privacy-utility trade-off and uncover three underlying mechanisms: Context-Dependent Utility, Strategic Adaptation, and Combinatorial Interplay. Guided by these insights, the authors introduce an intent-driven local protection framework powered by a distilled 4B model named Veilmind-4B that drives a dynamic extraction-sanitization-restoration pipeline. This approach achieves low privacy leakage while preserving higher response utility than existing baseline methods. The work advances privacy-preserving LLM deployment toward the Pareto frontier.
9beefa141aba5d6a:2309.one_liner: Veilmind-4B introduces an intent-driven dynamic sanitization pipeline to optimize the privacy-utility trade-off in LLM interactions.
9beefa141aba5d6a:2309.bottom_line: Context-aware, intent-driven sanitization frameworks outperform static privacy rules by preserving response utility while lowering data leakage.

claims.text: We introduce an intent-driven local protection framework driven by a lightweight model Veilmind-4B.

a9fc466a077b71f1:1829.summary: Semantic-gradient-based prompt optimization improves AI agent harnesses, but its local update rules leave edit scope and operations unresolved. The authors introduce RobustSGPO, a framework that specifies requested edits, checks generated patches, and manages search trajectories from incumbents or retained snapshots. Evaluations using the AgentX brainstorming workflow across 120 tasks show that periodic permission scheduling significantly outperforms fixed limits, increasing completion rates on held-out tasks and improving overall quality under token constraints. Category retention helps control source-task degradation after shifts, demonstrating that search-space controls improve agent harness evolution. This methodology offers developers structured control over automated prompt and harness optimization.

a9fc466a077b71f1:1829.bottom_line: Controlling search scope and scheduling permissions during semantic-gradient prompt optimization significantly boosts agent task completion rates.
